source_examples.japanese: 新しいレストランに行ってみよう。
source_examples.translation_en: Let's try going to the new restaurant.

source_examples.japanese: 映画を見てみたいです。
source_examples.translation_en: I want to try watching the movie.

source_title: Verb てもらいたい (～te moraitai)
source_short_explanation: Express a desire to receive a favor or service from someone else.
source_long_explanation: The ～てもらいたい grammar point is used to express one's desire to receive a favor, service, or action from someone else. It is formed by attaching もらいたい to the て-form of verbs. This structure emphasizes the help or favor the speaker wants from someone else.
source_formation: Verb-て-form + もらいたい

source_examples.japanese: この荷物を運んでもらいたいです。
source_examples.translation_en: I want you to carry this luggage for me.

source_examples.japanese: 彼にそのニュースを教えてもらいたい。
source_examples.translation_en: I want him to tell me the news.

source_examples.japanese: 友達に日本語を教えてもらいたい。
source_examples.translation_en: I want my friend to teach me Japanese.

source_examples.japanese: スタッフにチェックインの方法を説明してもらいたい。
source_examples.translation_en: I want the staff to explain the check-in process to me.

source_title: Verb て もらう (Verb-te morau)
source_short_explanation: Express receiving a favor or action from someone.
source_long_explanation: The Verb て もらう grammar point is used to express that the speaker or a third person receives a favor or action from someone else. It describes an action performed by someone for the benefit of the speaker or a third person, implying gratitude or request from the beneficiary.
source_formation: Verb-て form + もらう

source_examples.japanese: 友達に宿題を手伝ってもらった。
source_examples.translation_en: I had my friend help me with my homework.

source_examples.japanese: 母に部屋を掃除してもらいました。
source_examples.translation_en: I had my mother clean my room.

source_examples.japanese: 彼に荷物を持ってもらいたい。
source_examples.translation_en: I want him to carry my luggage for me.

source_examples.japanese: 先生に質問に答えてもらえますか？
source_examples.translation_en: Can I have the teacher answer my question?

source_title: Verb てもらえませんか (～te moraemasen ka)
source_short_explanation: A polite way to ask for a favor or request someone to do something.
source_long_explanation: The ～てもらえませんか grammar point is a polite and indirect way of asking someone to do something for you or asking for a favor. It is formed by conjugating the verb into the て-form and adding もらえませんか. This form is used in conversations to show politeness and humility.
source_formation: Verb-て form + もらえませんか

source_examples.japanese: この手紙を見てもらえませんか。
source_examples.translation_en: Could you take a look at this letter for me?

source_examples.japanese: 荷物を持ってもらえませんか。
source_examples.translation_en: Could you carry this luggage for me?

source_examples.japanese: 部屋を掃除してもらえませんか。
source_examples.translation_en: Could you clean the room for me?

source_examples.japanese: 明日のミーティングに参加してもらえませんか。
source_examples.translation_en: Could you attend tomorrow's meeting for me?

source_title: Verb ない ことがある (Verb-nai koto ga aru)
source_short_explanation: Expresses that something doesn't always happen or there are occasions when it doesn't happen.
source_long_explanation: The ないことがある grammar point is used to indicate that there are instances or times when something doesn't happen or isn't done. It is formed by combining the negative form of a verb (ない) with ことがある.
source_formation: Verb-negative form + ことがある

source_examples.japanese: 彼は会議に出席しないことがある。
source_examples.translation_en: There are times when he doesn't attend meetings.

source_examples.japanese: この電車は定刻に来ないことがある。
source_examples.translation_en: There are occasions when this train doesn't come on time.

source_examples.japanese: 私は朝食を食べないことがある。
source_examples.translation_en: There are times when I don't eat breakfast.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は電話に出ないことがある。
source_examples.translation_en: There are occasions when she doesn't answer the phone.

source_title: Verb ない + ことにする (Verb nai koto ni suru)
source_short_explanation: To decide not to do something.
source_long_explanation: The grammar point Verb ない + ことにする is used to express the decision not to do something. This structure shows that the speaker has made a conscious choice to not take the action expressed in the verb.
source_formation: Verb-ない form + ことにする

source_examples.japanese: 明日のパーティーに行かないことにする。
source_examples.translation_en: I've decided not to go to tomorrow's party.

source_examples.japanese: そのケーキを食べないことにします。
source_examples.translation_en: I've decided not to eat that cake.

source_examples.japanese: 今日はジョギングをしないことにする。
source_examples.translation_en: I've decided not to go jogging today.

source_examples.japanese: 彼と会わないことにしました。
source_examples.translation_en: I've decided not to meet him.

source_title: Verb ない ことになる (Verb nai koto ni naru)
source_short_explanation: Expresses a result; 'end up not', 'it will become that', 'it would mean that'.
source_long_explanation: The Verb ない ことになる grammar point is used to express a result or consequence. It translates to 'end up not', 'it will become that', or 'it would mean that' in English. It is formed by using the negative form (ない) of a verb followed by ことになる.
source_formation: Verb-negative (ない) + ことになる

source_examples.japanese: 今日彼が来ないことになると、私たちの予定はキャンセルされます。
source_examples.translation_en: If he doesn't come today, our plans will be canceled.

source_examples.japanese: このプロジェクトが進まないことになると、収益が減るでしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: If this project doesn't progress, it would mean that revenue will decrease.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は試験に合格しないことになると、卒業が遅れます。
source_examples.translation_en: If she ends up not passing the exam, her graduation will be delayed.

source_examples.japanese: 雨が降ると、ピクニックが行われないことになるでしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: If it rains, it will become that the picnic doesn't take place.

source_title: Verb ないほうがいい (Verb nai hou ga ii)
source_short_explanation: Expresses the idea that it is better not to do something.
source_long_explanation: The ないほうがいい grammar point is used to suggest that it's better not to do a certain action. It is formed by taking the negative form of the verb and adding ほうがいい.
source_formation: Verb-negative form + ほうがいい

source_examples.japanese: この薬は飲まないほうがいいです。
source_examples.translation_en: It's better not to take this medicine.

source_examples.japanese: 急いでいるときは、走らないほうがいい。
source_examples.translation_en: When you're in a hurry, it's better not to run.

source_examples.japanese: 彼に秘密を知られたくなければ、話さないほうがいい。
source_examples.translation_en: If you don't want him to know your secret, it's better not to tell him.

source_examples.japanese: 雨の日には、外出しないほうがいい。
source_examples.translation_en: It's better not to go out on a rainy day.

source_short_explanation: Expresses 'while' or 'as' in the sense of doing two things simultaneously.
source_long_explanation: The ～ながら grammar point is used to indicate that two actions are happening simultaneously or that one action is happening while another is taking place. This can be translated to 'while' or 'as' in English. It is primarily used with verbs.
source_formation: Verb-masu stem + ながら

source_examples.japanese: テレビを見ながら宿題をしました。
source_examples.translation_en: I did my homework while watching television.

source_examples.japanese: 音楽を聞きながら料理をしました。
source_examples.translation_en: I cooked while listening to music.

source_examples.japanese: 歩きながらスマホを見るのは危険です。
source_examples.translation_en: Looking at your smartphone while walking is dangerous.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は話しながら笑っていました。
source_examples.translation_en: He was laughing while talking.

source_short_explanation: A command form used to give orders or instructions; 'Please do', 'Do this'.
source_long_explanation: The なさい grammar point is used to give orders or instructions, often used by teachers, parents, or other authority figures when addressing someone younger or of lower status. It is formed by attaching なさい to the stem of a verb. This form sounds polite, but can be considered strong and direct.
source_formation: Verb-stem + なさい

source_examples.japanese: 部屋を掃除しなさい。
source_examples.translation_en: Clean your room.

source_examples.japanese: 勉強しなさい。
source_examples.translation_en: Study.

source_examples.japanese: 早く起きなさい。
source_examples.translation_en: Wake up early.

source_examples.japanese: 宿題をやりなさい。
source_examples.translation_en: Do your homework.

source_short_explanation: Express difficulty or complexity; 'hard to', 'difficult to', 'not easily'.
source_long_explanation: The ～にくい grammar point is used to express that an action is difficult or relatively hard to do. It is used by attaching にくい to the stem of a verb. It can be translated as 'hard to', 'difficult to', or 'not easily' in English.
source_formation: Verb-stem + にくい

source_examples.japanese: この字は読みにくいです。
source_examples.translation_en: This character is hard to read.

source_examples.japanese: このドアは開けにくい。
source_examples.translation_en: This door is difficult to open.

source_examples.japanese: 彼の字は読みにくい。
source_examples.translation_en: His handwriting is hard to read.

source_examples.japanese: この料理は作りにくい。
source_examples.translation_en: This dish is difficult to make.

source_short_explanation: Indicates that something is easy to do; 'easy to', 'easy for'.
source_long_explanation: The やすい grammar point is used to express that something is easy to do or easy for someone. It is attached to the verb stem and can be translated as 'easy to' or 'easy for' in English. This formation is used with verbs only.
source_formation: Verb-stem + やすい

source_examples.japanese: この本は読みやすいです。
source_examples.translation_en: This book is easy to read.

source_examples.japanese: このシャツは着やすい。
source_examples.translation_en: This shirt is easy to wear.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は話しやすい人です。
source_examples.translation_en: He is an easy person to talk to.

source_examples.japanese: この料理は作りやすい。
source_examples.translation_en: This dish is easy to make.

source_title: Verb ようと思う (Verb-you to omou)
source_short_explanation: Express intention or plan to do something; 'I think I will', 'I plan to', 'I intend to'.
source_long_explanation: The ようと思う grammar point is used to express the intention or plan to do something in the future. It can be translated as 'I think I will', 'I plan to', or 'I intend to' in English. The formation involves using the volitional form of the verb followed by と思う.
source_formation: Verb-volitional + と思う

source_examples.japanese: 明日、映画を見ようと思います。
source_examples.translation_en: I think I will watch a movie tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: 週末に友達と遊ぼうと思っています。
source_examples.translation_en: I plan to hang out with friends on the weekend.

source_examples.japanese: 勉強をもっと頑張ろうと思う。
source_examples.translation_en: I intend to study harder.

source_examples.japanese: 来年は海外旅行に行こうと思っている。
source_examples.translation_en: I plan to go on an overseas trip next year.

source_short_explanation: Used to express 'like', 'as if', 'in order to', or 'so that'.
source_long_explanation: The ～ように grammar point is used to express different meanings depending on the context: 'like', 'as if', 'in order to', or 'so that'. Formation patterns can include: Noun + のように, Verb dictionary/negative form + ように, い-adjective + ように, etc.
source_formation: Examples: Noun + のように / Verb-casual + ように / い-adjective + ように

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は鳥のように軽やかに踊る。
source_examples.translation_en: She dances lightly like a bird.

source_examples.japanese: 覚えたことを忘れないように、毎日復習しましょう。
source_examples.translation_en: In order not to forget what you've learned, let's review every day.

source_examples.japanese: 歌手になるように、毎日歌の練習をしています。
source_examples.translation_en: In order to become a singer, I practice singing every day.

source_examples.japanese: 道を渡る時、車が来ないように確認してください。
source_examples.translation_en: When crossing the road, please make sure no cars are coming.

source_title: Verb ようにする (Verb ~you ni suru)
source_short_explanation: Make an effort to; try to; see to it that; ensure that.
source_long_explanation: The ようにする grammar point is used to express that someone is making an effort, trying, or seeing to it that something happens. It can be translated as 'make sure to', 'try to', or 'ensure that' in English. The formation is simple, involving a verb in the dictionary form followed by ようにする.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + ようにする

source_examples.japanese: 毎日運動するようにしています。
source_examples.translation_en: I try to exercise every day.

source_examples.japanese: 早く寝るようにしてください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please try to go to bed early.

source_examples.japanese: 約束を守るようにします。
source_examples.translation_en: I will make sure to keep my promise.

source_examples.japanese: 彼に会わないようにする。
source_examples.translation_en: I will try not to see him.

source_title: Verb ようになる (〜you ni naru)
source_short_explanation: Express a change in ability, situation or state; 'become able to', 'come to', 'begin to'.
source_long_explanation: The ようになる grammar implies a change or development involving new abilities, situations or states. It can be translated into English as 'become able to', 'come to' or 'begin to'. This grammar is often used when talking about a skill that has been acquired or a change in habit or situation over time.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary/potential form + ようになる

source_examples.japanese: 日本語が話せるようになりました。
source_examples.translation_en: I have become able to speak Japanese.

source_examples.japanese: 最近、早く寝るようになった。
source_examples.translation_en: Recently, I have come to go to bed early.

source_examples.japanese: 彼はピアノを弾けるようになりました。
source_examples.translation_en: He has become able to play the piano.

source_examples.japanese: この仕事を始めてから、毎日忙しいと感じるようになりました。
source_examples.translation_en: Since I started this job, I've begun to feel busy every day.

source_title: Verb ように言う (Verb-you ni iu)
source_short_explanation: Tell someone to do something; 'tell to do', 'instruct to do'.
source_long_explanation: The grammar point Verb ように言う is used when someone tells or instructs another person to do something. It can be translated as 'tell to do' or 'instruct to do' in English. The formation is created by adding ように言う to the casual form of a verb.
source_formation: Verb-casual + ように言う

source_examples.japanese: 先生は私たちに宿題をやるように言いました。
source_examples.translation_en: The teacher told us to do our homework.

source_examples.japanese: 母は弟に部屋を片付けるように言いました。
source_examples.translation_en: My mother told my younger brother to clean his room.

source_examples.japanese: 上司は私に報告書を提出するように言いました。
source_examples.translation_en: My boss told me to submit the report.

source_examples.japanese: 友達が私に早く来るように言いました。
source_examples.translation_en: My friend told me to come early.

source_short_explanation: Expresses passive voice or potential form for verbs.
source_long_explanation: The られる grammar point can be used to express passive voice or potential form for verbs. Passive voice indicates that the action is being done to the subject, while potential form expresses the ability or possibility to do an action. The formation of られる depends on the type of verb (う, る, or irregular verbs).
source_formation: う-verb (passive): Replace the final う with われる / る-verb (passive & potential): Replace る with られる / Irregular: する → される, くる → こられる

source_examples.japanese: 彼は先生に褒められました。
source_examples.translation_en: He was praised by the teacher.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は友達に笑われました。
source_examples.translation_en: He was laughed at by his friends.

source_examples.japanese: 映画は観られましたか？
source_examples.translation_en: Were you able to watch the movie?

source_examples.japanese: 彼女はリーダーに選ばれました。
source_examples.translation_en: She was chosen as the leader.

source_title: Verb る ことがある (〜ru koto ga aru)
source_short_explanation: Used to express that something happens sometimes or has happened before.
source_long_explanation: The grammar point る ことがある is used to express that something occurs sometimes or has occurred in the past. It indicates that the action is not a regular or constant event, but rather something that takes place occasionally or has happened at least once.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + ことがある

source_examples.japanese: 彼は遅刻することがあります。
source_examples.translation_en: He is sometimes late.

source_examples.japanese: 私は寝坊することがあります。
source_examples.translation_en: I sometimes oversleep.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は歌を歌うことがあります。
source_examples.translation_en: She sometimes sings songs.

source_examples.japanese: 子供の頃、よく山に登ることがありました。
source_examples.translation_en: When I was a child, I sometimes climbed mountains.

source_title: Verb ることにする (〜ru koto ni suru)
source_short_explanation: Decide to do something, make a decision.
source_long_explanation: The ～ることにする grammar point is used to express that someone has made a decision to do something or has decided on a specific course of action. It is formed by attaching ことにする to the verb in its る form.
source_formation: Verb-る + ことにする

source_examples.japanese: 来週、ジムに行くことにしました。
source_examples.translation_en: I decided to go to the gym next week.

source_examples.japanese: この靴を買うことにしました。
source_examples.translation_en: I decided to buy these shoes.

source_examples.japanese: 毎日、散歩をすることにしました。
source_examples.translation_en: I decided to take a walk every day.

source_examples.japanese: 彼に電話をかけることにします。
source_examples.translation_en: I’ve decided to call him.

source_title: Verb る ことになる (〜ru koto ni naru)
source_short_explanation: Indicates that something has been decided or arranged; 'it has been decided that', 'it turns out that'.
source_long_explanation: The る ことになる grammar point is used to express that something has been decided or arranged. It often indicates a decision made by someone else or due to circumstances. It can be translated as 'it has been decided that' or 'it turns out that' in English. The formation requires a verb in る (dictionary) form.
source_formation: Verb-る + ことになる

source_examples.japanese: 今日は会議がなくなることになりました。
source_examples.translation_en: It has been decided that there will be no meeting today.

source_examples.japanese: 来週、友達と旅行することになった。
source_examples.translation_en: It has been arranged that I will travel with my friends next week.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女が今度のプロジェクトのリーダーになることになりました。
source_examples.translation_en: It has been decided that she will be the leader of the next project.

source_examples.japanese: 急に仕事が入ったので、休みを取ることになった。
source_examples.translation_en: Due to sudden work, it has been decided that I will take a day off.

source_title: Verb るときに (〜ru toki ni)
source_short_explanation: Describes the time when a certain action takes place; 'when', 'at the time'.
source_long_explanation: The ～るときに grammar point is used to indicate the time when a certain action or event happens. It can be translated as 'when' or 'at the time' in English. The formation involves attaching ときに to the verb in its dictionary (る) form.
source_formation: Verb-る + ときに

source_examples.japanese: 映画を見るときに、ポップコーンを食べます。
source_examples.translation_en: When I watch a movie, I eat popcorn.

source_examples.japanese: 寝るときに、部屋の電気を消します。
source_examples.translation_en: When I go to bed, I turn off the room lights.

source_examples.japanese: 運動するときに、水分補給が大切です。
source_examples.translation_en: When exercising, it's important to stay hydrated.

source_examples.japanese: 旅行するときに、カメラを持っていくことが好きです。
source_examples.translation_en: When I travel, I like to bring a camera.

source_title: Verb る ところ (Verb-ru tokoro)
source_short_explanation: Expresses the state or moment when an action is about to happen or is happening.
source_long_explanation: The grammar point 'Verb る ところ' is used to express that one is just about to do something, or is in the process of doing it. It can be translated as 'just about to' or 'in the middle of' in English, depending on context.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + ところ

source_examples.japanese: 彼は食べるところです。
source_examples.translation_en: He is in the process of eating.

source_examples.japanese: 私は出かけるところです。
source_examples.translation_en: I am just about to leave.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は泣くところでした。
source_examples.translation_en: She was on the verge of crying.

source_examples.japanese: 私たちは勉強するところです。
source_examples.translation_en: We are in the middle of studying.

source_short_explanation: Express the action of taking something out, starting an action, or emphasizing a verb.
source_long_explanation: The verb 出す (~dasu) is used to express the action of taking something out, starting an action, or emphasizing the verb it is attached to. To form this grammar point, simply attach 出す (~dasu) to the stem of the verb.
source_formation: Verb stem + 出す (~dasu)

source_examples.japanese: 本を棚から出してください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please take the book out from the shelf.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は部屋から急いで出ました。
source_examples.translation_en: He rushed out of the room.

source_examples.japanese: 授業が始まる前に宿題を出してください。
source_examples.translation_en: Submit your homework before class starts.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は歌い出しました。
source_examples.translation_en: She began to sing.

source_short_explanation: Indicates the way or method of doing something; often read as '～かた' ('how to', 'the way of').
source_long_explanation: The ～方 grammar point is used to express the way or method of doing something, similar to 'how to' or 'the way of' in English. It can be attached to the stem of a verb to form a noun that indicates the method of doing the action. In practice, ～方 is usually read as '～かた' (e.g., 作り方＝つくりかた).
source_formation: Verb-stem + 方 (read as かた)

source_examples.japanese: 誰かがケーキの作り方を知っていますか？
source_examples.translation_en: Does anyone know how to make a cake?

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は英語の話し方を学んでいます。
source_examples.translation_en: She is learning how to speak English.

source_examples.japanese: このパソコンの使い方を教えてください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please teach me how to use this computer.

source_examples.japanese: 数学の問題の解き方を覚えるのが難しいです。
source_examples.translation_en: It is difficult to remember the way to solve math problems.

source_short_explanation: Verbal action is completed; 'to finish', 'to end'.
source_long_explanation: The verb 終わる (owaru) is used to express that an action has been completed or something has come to an end. Despite ending in る, 終わる is a godan (u-verb), so it does not follow the typical ichidan (る-verb) conjugation. It is translated as 'to finish', 'to end' or 'to be over' in English.
source_formation: 終わる (owaru) is a godan (u-verb)

source_examples.japanese: 映画が終わったら、家に帰ります。
source_examples.translation_en: When the movie finishes, I'll go home.

source_examples.japanese: 仕事が終わるまで、待ってください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please wait until the work is finished.

source_examples.japanese: パーティーはもうすぐ終わります。
source_examples.translation_en: The party will be over soon.

source_examples.japanese: 試験が終わったら、友達と遊びに行く予定です。
source_examples.translation_en: Once the exam is over, I plan to go out with my friends.

source_title: Verb + 続ける (つづける, tsuzukeru)
source_short_explanation: To continue doing or to keep doing an action.
source_long_explanation: The grammar point 続ける (tsuzukeru) is attached to the masu-stem form of verbs, and it indicates the ongoing continuity of an action. It can be translated as 'to continue doing' or 'to keep doing' in English.
source_formation: Verb-masu-stem + 続ける

source_examples.japanese: 彼は毎日ジムで運動を続けています。
source_examples.translation_en: He continues to exercise at the gym every day.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は勉強を続けるために図書館に行きました。
source_examples.translation_en: She went to the library to continue studying.

source_examples.japanese: 私たちは雨にも関わらず散歩を続けました。
source_examples.translation_en: We continued walking despite the rain.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は仕事を続けることに決めた。
source_examples.translation_en: He decided to continue working.

source_short_explanation: Indicates uncertainty or doubt; 'I wonder', 'I'm not sure'.
source_long_explanation: The ～かしら grammar point is used to express uncertainty or doubt about a situation. It can be translated as 'I wonder' or 'I'm not sure' in English. It is primarily used by females in casual conversations but can be used by males in some contexts as well. ～かしら is used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
source_formation: Verb-casual + かしら, い-Adjective + かしら, な-Adjective + かしら, Noun + かしら

source_examples.japanese: 今日は雨が降るかしら？
source_examples.translation_en: I wonder if it will rain today?

source_examples.japanese: このケーキは美味しいかしら？
source_examples.translation_en: I wonder if this cake is delicious?

source_examples.japanese: 彼は病気かしら？
source_examples.translation_en: I wonder if he is sick?

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は学生かしら？
source_examples.translation_en: I wonder if she is a student?

source_short_explanation: Used to express 'whether' or 'if' in indirect questions or statements.
source_long_explanation: The ～かどうか grammar point is used to express 'whether' or 'if' in indirect questions or statements. It is often used to express uncertainty or to inquire about information in a more polite form. ～かどうか can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
source_formation: Verb-casual + かどうか, い-Adjective + かどうか, な-Adjective + (だ)かどうか, Noun + (だ)かどうか

source_examples.japanese: 彼が来るかどうか知りません。
source_examples.translation_en: I don't know if he will come or not.

source_examples.japanese: この本が面白いかどうか教えてください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please tell me if this book is interesting or not.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女が綺麗だかどうかは分かりません。
source_examples.translation_en: I don't know whether she is beautiful or not.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が先生だかどうか覚えていません。
source_examples.translation_en: I don't remember if he is a teacher or not.

source_short_explanation: Expresses uncertainty or wonder; 'I wonder', 'I'm not sure'.
source_long_explanation: The ～かなあ grammar point is used to express a feeling of uncertainty or wonder about a situation or statement. It can be translated as 'I wonder' or 'I'm not sure' in English. In casual spoken Japanese, when using nouns or な-adjectives before かなあ, the copula だ is often omitted or replaced with の (e.g., 学生かなあ or 学生なのかなあ). This grammar point should not be used when asking questions directly to someone, as it may come off as too direct or impolite.
source_formation: Verb-casual + かなあ, い-Adjective + かなあ, (な-Adjective/Noun) + (だ) + かなあ

source_examples.japanese: 明日雨が降るかなあ。
source_examples.translation_en: I wonder if it will rain tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: このケーキは美味しいかなあ。
source_examples.translation_en: I wonder if this cake is delicious.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は病気かなあ。
source_examples.translation_en: I wonder if he is sick.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は学生かなあ。
source_examples.translation_en: I wonder if she is a student.

source_short_explanation: Express uncertainty; 'maybe', 'might', 'possibly'.
source_long_explanation: The ～かもしれない grammar point is used to express uncertainty or the possibility of something occurring. It can be translated as 'maybe', 'might', or 'possibly' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun. In everyday speech, speakers often omit だ before かもしれない for nouns and な-adjectives.
source_formation: Verb-casual + かもしれない, い-Adjective + かもしれない, な-Adjective + だかもしれない, Noun + だかもしれない

source_examples.japanese: 明日雨が降るかもしれない。
source_examples.translation_en: It might rain tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: このケーキは美味しいかもしれない。
source_examples.translation_en: This cake might be delicious.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が病気かもしれない。
source_examples.translation_en: He might be sick.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は学生かもしれない。
source_examples.translation_en: She might be a student.

source_short_explanation: Express a polite request to allow or permit someone to do something.
source_long_explanation: The ～させてください grammar point is used to make a polite request to allow or permit someone to do something. It can be translated as 'please let me' or 'please allow me to' in English. It is formed by taking the causative form of a verb and adding ください.
source_formation: Verb-causative form + ください

source_examples.japanese: もう少し考えさせてください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please let me think a little more.

source_examples.japanese: 写真を撮らせてください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please let me take a photo.

source_examples.japanese: もうちょっと練習させてください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please let me practice a little more.

source_examples.japanese: ここで待たせてください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please let me wait here.

source_short_explanation: Express multiple reasons or characteristics; 'and', 'because', 'since'.
source_long_explanation: The ～し、～し、～ grammar point is used to connect multiple reasons or characteristics that support a conclusion or statement. It can be translated as 'and', 'because', or 'since' in English. This grammar can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
source_formation: Verb-casual + し, い-Adjective + し, な-Adjective + だし, Noun + だし

source_examples.japanese: 彼は若いし、元気だし、フレンドリーだし、みんなと仲良くなれると思います。
source_examples.translation_en: He is young, energetic, friendly, and I think he can get along with everyone.

source_examples.japanese: このレストランは料理が美味しいし、雰囲気がいいし、価格も手頃だからお勧めです。
source_examples.translation_en: I recommend this restaurant because the food is delicious, the atmosphere is nice, and the prices are reasonable.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は勉強ができるし、スポーツも得意だし、性格もいい。
source_examples.translation_en: She is good at studying, good at sports, and has a good personality.

source_examples.japanese: 今日は寒いし、雨も降っているし、家でゆっくり休んだ方がいいでしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: It's cold today, and it's raining, so it's better to relax at home.

source_short_explanation: Expresses that something is excessive or overdone; 'too much', 'too', 'over'.
source_long_explanation: The ～すぎる grammar point is used to express that something is excessive or beyond a certain level. It can be translated as 'too much', 'too', or 'over' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, or な-adjective.
source_formation: Verb-stem + すぎる, い-Adjective (remove い) + すぎる, な-Adjective + すぎる

source_examples.japanese: この部屋は暑すぎる。
source_examples.translation_en: This room is too hot.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は早く来すぎた。
source_examples.translation_en: He came too early.

source_examples.japanese: この箱は重すぎて持ち上げられない。
source_examples.translation_en: This box is too heavy to lift.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は忙しくて遊びすぎはしない。
source_examples.translation_en: She's too busy to play too much.

source_short_explanation: Indicates equal distribution; 'each', 'per', 'apiece'.
source_long_explanation: The ～ずつ grammar point is used to express an equal distribution of something, whether it is an action, an amount, or an item. It is translated as 'each', 'per', or 'apiece' in English.
source_formation: Noun + ずつ

source_examples.japanese: りんごを2つずつ配ります。
source_examples.translation_en: I will distribute 2 apples each.

source_examples.japanese: 私たちは週に一度ずつ掃除をします。
source_examples.translation_en: We each clean once per week.

source_examples.japanese: みんなは同じ距離を一歩ずつ歩いた。
source_examples.translation_en: Everyone walked the same distance, one step at a time.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は子供たちに一枚ずつプレゼントをくれました。
source_examples.translation_en: She gave one present to each child.

source_short_explanation: Express the appearance, seeming, or feeling of something; 'looks like', 'seems', 'appears'.
source_long_explanation: The ～そうだ grammar point is used to describe the appearance or feeling of something based on what is observed or inferred. It can be translated as 'looks like', 'seems', or 'appears' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, or な-adjective.
source_formation: Verb-ますstem + そうだ, い-Adjective (without い) + そうだ, な-Adjective + そうだ

source_examples.japanese: その花はとてもきれいそうだ。
source_examples.translation_en: That flower looks very beautiful.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は疲れそうだ。
source_examples.translation_en: He looks tired.

source_examples.japanese: この本は面白そうだ。
source_examples.translation_en: This book looks interesting.

source_examples.japanese: 雨が降りそうだ。
source_examples.translation_en: It looks like it's going to rain.

source_short_explanation: Expresses 'that kind/type of'; referring to something near the listener or previously mentioned.
source_long_explanation: The word 'そんな' is used before a noun to indicate 'that kind of' or 'that type of', typically referring to something near the listener or previously mentioned in the conversation. It specifies the noun based on context or shared understanding between the speaker and the listener.
source_formation: そんな + Noun

source_examples.japanese: そんな話、信じられない。
source_examples.translation_en: I can't believe that kind of story.

source_examples.japanese: そんな映画、見たくない。
source_examples.translation_en: I don't want to watch that kind of movie.

source_short_explanation: Expresses 'not so much', 'not that', or 'not so ~'.
source_long_explanation: The grammar point そんなに is an adverb used to express that something is not as extreme as described or not to that extent. It is often translated as 'not so much', 'not that', or 'not so ~'. It is commonly followed by a negative form of a verb or adjective.
source_formation: そんなに + Verb-negation, そんなに + Adjective-negation

source_examples.japanese: そんなに急がなくてもいいですよ。
source_examples.translation_en: You don't have to hurry that much.

source_examples.japanese: そんなに難しくない問題だと思います。
source_examples.translation_en: I don't think the problem is that difficult.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女はそんなに背が高くありません。
source_examples.translation_en: She is not that tall.

source_examples.japanese: そんなにたくさん食べる必要はないと思う。
source_examples.translation_en: I don't think there's a need to eat so much.

source_short_explanation: Expressing a desire or suggestion for a particular outcome; 'it would be good if', 'should', 'I hope'.
source_long_explanation: The ～たらいい grammar point is used to express a desire, suggestion, or hope for a particular outcome. It can be translated as 'it would be good if', 'should', or 'I hope' in English. The formation is simple, and it is used with verbs in their casual past tense form.
source_formation: Verb-casual-past + たらいい

source_examples.japanese: もっと勉強したらいいですよ。
source_examples.translation_en: It would be good if you studied more.

source_examples.japanese: 雨が止んだらいいな。
source_examples.translation_en: I hope the rain stops.

source_examples.japanese: 早く元気になったらいいですね。
source_examples.translation_en: It would be good if you got well soon.

source_examples.japanese: 彼に連絡したらいいと思います。
source_examples.translation_en: I think it would be good if you contacted him.

source_title: ～たら いかがですか (〜tara ikaga desu ka)
source_short_explanation: Making polite suggestions; 'how about if', 'what if', 'it would be good if'.
source_long_explanation: The ～たら いかがですか grammar point is used to make polite suggestions, ask for opinions, or imply that something would be good or desirable if the condition is met. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
source_formation: Verb-casual, past + たら いかがですか, い-Adjective + かったら いかがですか, な-Adjective + だったら いかがですか, Noun + だったら いかがですか

source_examples.japanese: 図書館に行ったらいかがですか。
source_examples.translation_en: How about going to the library?

source_examples.japanese: 寒かったらカーディガンを着るのはいかがですか。
source_examples.translation_en: How about wearing a cardigan if it's cold?

source_examples.japanese: 部屋が暗かったら照明を付けるのはいかがですか。
source_examples.translation_en: What if you turn on the light if the room is dark?

source_examples.japanese: 自分の意見だったら他人に聞くのはいかがですか。
source_examples.translation_en: How about asking others if it's your own opinion?

source_short_explanation: Express a suggestion or advice; 'what if', 'how about', 'why don't you'.
source_long_explanation: The ～たら どうですか grammar point is used to make a suggestion or give advice to someone. It can be translated as 'what if', 'how about', or 'why don't you' in English. This structure is used with the た-form of verbs to make a gentle, polite suggestion.
source_formation: Verb-た form + ら どうですか

source_examples.japanese: スキーに行ったらどうですか？
source_examples.translation_en: How about going skiing?

source_examples.japanese: 少し休んだらどうですか？
source_examples.translation_en: What if you take a little break?

source_examples.japanese: この本を読んだらどうですか？
source_examples.translation_en: Why don't you read this book?

source_examples.japanese: タクシーで帰ったらどうですか？
source_examples.translation_en: How about going home by taxi?

source_short_explanation: Used to list multiple actions or states; 'doing things like', 'and so on', 'etc.'
source_long_explanation: The ～たり～たり grammar point is used to list two or more actions or states, without specifying their order or importance. It implies that these actions or states are representative examples, and there may be others. This construction is useful for describing general or habitual actions.
source_formation: Verb-ta + り + next verb-ta + り, い-Adjective + かったり + next verb-ta + り, な-Adjective + だったり + next verb-ta + り, Noun + だったり + next verb-ta + り

source_examples.japanese: 週末は映画を観たり、本を読んだりする。
source_examples.translation_en: On weekends, I do things like watching movies and reading books.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は料理が上手だったり、歌がうまかったりする。
source_examples.translation_en: She is good at things like cooking and singing.

source_examples.japanese: このリゾートではスキーをしたり、温泉に入ったりできる。
source_examples.translation_en: At this resort, you can do things like skiing and going to hot springs.

source_examples.japanese: この地域の天気は暑かったり、寒かったりする。
source_examples.translation_en: The weather in this area can be hot or cold.

source_short_explanation: Express probability, likelihood or certainty; 'probably', 'maybe', 'I think'.
source_long_explanation: The ～だろう grammar point is used to express probability, likelihood, or certainty about a situation or event. It can be translated as 'probably', 'maybe', or 'I think' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
source_formation: Verb-casual + だろう, い-Adjective (drop い) + だろう, な-Adjective + だろう, Noun + だろう

source_examples.japanese: 明日は晴れるだろう。
source_examples.translation_en: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は忙しいだろう。
source_examples.translation_en: He is probably busy.

source_examples.japanese: この本は面白いだろう。
source_examples.translation_en: This book is probably interesting.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は先生だろう。
source_examples.translation_en: She is probably a teacher.

source_short_explanation: Used to quote, define, or specify a noun.
source_long_explanation: The ～っていう grammar point is used for quoting, defining, or specifying a noun. It can be translated as 'called', 'that is to say', or 'I mean' in English. This expression is similar to ～という, but it is more casual and commonly used in spoken conversations.
source_formation: Noun/Adjective/Verb + っていう + Noun

source_examples.japanese: ピザっていう料理が大好きです。
source_examples.translation_en: I love the dish called pizza.

source_examples.japanese: 彼っていう男性はすごく面白いです。
source_examples.translation_en: That man (called ‘kare’) is really interesting.

source_examples.japanese: この映画っていうのは本当に感動的だよ。
source_examples.translation_en: This movie, I mean, is really touching.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女が言っているっていう店はここではない。
source_examples.translation_en: The store she's talking about, I mean, is not here.

source_short_explanation: Indicates the means, method, or place.
source_long_explanation: The ～で grammar point is used to indicate the means or method used to perform an action, or to specify the place where an action took place. It is typically used with verbs and comes after a noun.
source_formation: Noun + ～で

source_examples.japanese: 私は自転車で学校に行きます。
source_examples.translation_en: I go to school by bicycle.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は日本語で手紙を書いた。
source_examples.translation_en: He wrote a letter in Japanese.

source_examples.japanese: 鉛筆で絵を描きました。
source_examples.translation_en: I drew a picture with a pencil.

source_examples.japanese: レストランで昼食を食べました。
source_examples.translation_en: I had lunch at a restaurant.

source_short_explanation: A conjecture or probability; 'probably', 'I think', 'it seems'.
source_long_explanation: The ～でしょう grammar point is used to indicate a conjecture or probability. It can be translated as 'probably', 'I think', or 'it seems' in English. It can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
source_formation: Verb-ますstem + でしょう, い-Adjective + でしょう, な-Adjective + でしょう, Noun + でしょう

source_examples.japanese: 明日は晴れでしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は元気でしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: He is probably fine.

source_examples.japanese: この本は面白いでしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: This book is probably interesting.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は医者でしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: She is probably a doctor.

source_short_explanation: Expresses prohibition; 'must not', 'cannot'.
source_long_explanation: The ～てはいけない grammar point is used to express strict prohibition or something that must not be done. It can be translated as 'must not', 'cannot', or 'should not' in English. It is formed by adding て-form of a verb followed by はいけない.
source_formation: Verb-て-form + はいけない

source_examples.japanese: 公園でたばこを吸ってはいけない。
source_examples.translation_en: You must not smoke in the park.

source_examples.japanese: ここで写真を撮ってはいけない。
source_examples.translation_en: You cannot take pictures here.

source_examples.japanese: 図書館で大きな声を出してはいけない。
source_examples.translation_en: You must not speak loudly in the library.

source_examples.japanese: バスの中で立っている人に席を譲ってはいけない。(Note: Unusual in real life, but grammatically correct.)
source_examples.translation_en: You should not give up your seat to someone standing on the bus. (Note: Odd in actual social context, but valid grammar.)

source_short_explanation: To give or ask permission; 'it's okay to', 'may', 'can'.
source_long_explanation: The ～てもいい grammar point is used to give or ask for permission to do something. It can be translated as 'it's okay to', 'may', or 'can' in English. The formation is derived by adding てもいい after the て-form of a verb.
source_formation: Verb-て form + もいい

source_examples.japanese: ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか。
source_examples.translation_en: Is it okay to take a photo here?

source_examples.japanese: このリンゴを食べてもいいですか。
source_examples.translation_en: May I eat this apple?

source_examples.japanese: 試験が終わったら、帰ってもいいです。
source_examples.translation_en: You can go home after the exam is over.

source_examples.japanese: 今夜友達と遊んでもいい。
source_examples.translation_en: It's okay to play with friends tonight.

source_short_explanation: Expresses 'even if' or 'even though'; used to convey contradiction or contrast.
source_long_explanation: The ～ても/でも grammar point is used to express 'even if' or 'even though' in a sentence, showing the idea of contradiction or contrast. The formation of ても differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, or な-adjective. For nouns, でも is used.
source_formation: Verb-て-form + も, い-Adjective (-い) + くても, な-Adjective + でも, Noun + でも

source_examples.japanese: 雨が降っても、学校に行きます。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if it rains, I will go to school.

source_examples.japanese: この部屋が汚くても、掃除しないつもりです。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if this room is dirty, I don't intend to clean it.

source_examples.japanese: その映画が面白くなくても、見ます。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if that movie is not interesting, I will watch it.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女が病気でも、働きます。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if she is sick, she will work.

source_short_explanation: Express a wish or hope; 'I hope', 'it would be good if'.
source_long_explanation: The ～といい grammar point is used to express a wish or hope for a certain situation or outcome. It can be translated as 'I hope', 'it would be good if', or 'it would be nice if' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
source_formation: Verb-casual + といい, い-Adjective + といい, な-Adjective + だといい, Noun + だといい

source_examples.japanese: 明日晴れるといいね。
source_examples.translation_en: I hope it will be sunny tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: この試験に合格するといい。
source_examples.translation_en: I hope to pass this exam.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が元気だといいな。
source_examples.translation_en: I hope he is doing well.

source_examples.japanese: そのレストランが美味しいといいですね。
source_examples.translation_en: It would be nice if that restaurant is delicious.

source_short_explanation: Used to define or explain a noun more specifically.
source_long_explanation: The ～という grammar point is used to define or explain a noun more specifically. It is often translated as 'called', 'named', or 'that is to say' in English. It can be used with nouns, な-adjectives, and adjectival verbs.
source_formation: Noun + という + Noun, な-Adjective + という + Noun, Adjectival Verb + という + Noun

source_examples.japanese: 彼は日本語が流暢なアメリカ人という人です。
source_examples.translation_en: He is an American who speaks fluent Japanese.

source_examples.japanese: 昨日、美味しかったというケーキを食べました。
source_examples.translation_en: Yesterday, I ate a cake that was said to be delicious.

source_examples.japanese: 有名な歌手という彼女は、たくさんのファンがいます。
source_examples.translation_en: She, who is called a famous singer, has many fans.

source_examples.japanese: 環境に優しいという製品が人気があります。
source_examples.translation_en: Products that are said to be environmentally friendly are popular.

source_title: どういう Noun (dou iu Noun)
source_short_explanation: Asking for clarification or more information about a noun; 'what kind of', 'what sort of'.
source_long_explanation: The どういう Noun grammar point is used to ask for more information or clarification about a specific noun. It can be translated as 'what kind of' or 'what sort of' in English. The formation is simply using どういう followed by the noun in question.
source_formation: どういう + Noun

source_examples.japanese: どういう仕事をしていますか？
source_examples.translation_en: What kind of work do you do?

source_examples.japanese: どういう映画が好きですか？
source_examples.translation_en: What kind of movies do you like?

source_examples.japanese: どういう服を着たいですか？
source_examples.translation_en: What kind of clothes do you want to wear?

source_examples.japanese: どういう理由で遅れましたか？
source_examples.translation_en: What sort of reason caused you to be late?

source_short_explanation: Express one's thoughts or opinions; 'I think', 'I believe'.
source_long_explanation: The ～と思う grammar point is used to express one's thoughts or opinions on a particular subject or situation. It can be translated as 'I think' or 'I believe' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
source_formation: Verb-casual + と思う, い-Adjective + と思う, な-Adjective + だと思う, Noun + だと思う

source_examples.japanese: 明日晴れると思います。
source_examples.translation_en: I think it will be sunny tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: この映画は面白いと思う。
source_examples.translation_en: I think this movie is interesting.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は親切だと思います。
source_examples.translation_en: I think he is kind.

source_examples.japanese: 鈴木さんは先生だと思う。
source_examples.translation_en: I think Suzuki-san is a teacher.

source_short_explanation: Used to quote, express hearsay or define something.
source_long_explanation: The ～という grammar point is used to quote someone's words, express something you heard or read from someone else, or define and clarify the subject. It can be translated as 'called', 'that', or 'it is said'. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
source_formation: Verb-casual + という, い-Adjective + という, な-Adjective + という, Noun + という

source_examples.japanese: 彼は「好きだ」と言った。
source_examples.translation_en: He said 'I like you'.

source_examples.japanese: その映画は面白いという評判があります。
source_examples.translation_en: The movie has a reputation for being interesting.

source_examples.japanese: 日本には富士山という高い山があります。
source_examples.translation_en: In Japan, there is a tall mountain called Mount Fuji.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は難しい仕事をしているという話です。
source_examples.translation_en: I heard she is doing a difficult job.

source_short_explanation: Express a necessity; 'must', 'have to', 'need to'.
source_long_explanation: The ～ないといけない grammar point is used to express a sense of necessity or obligation, similar to 'must', 'have to', or 'need to' in English. This structure is formed by using the negative form of the verb (ending in ない) followed by といけない.
source_formation: Verb-negative + といけない

source_examples.japanese: 明日試験があるから、今夜勉強しないといけない。
source_examples.translation_en: I have an exam tomorrow, so I have to study tonight.

source_examples.japanese: ９時に出発しないといけない。
source_examples.translation_en: We must leave at 9 o'clock.

source_examples.japanese: 風邪をひかないように、手をよく洗わないといけない。
source_examples.translation_en: To avoid catching a cold, we have to wash our hands well.

source_examples.japanese: この仕事は明日までに終わらないといけない。
source_examples.translation_en: This work must be finished by tomorrow.

source_short_explanation: Express a necessity or obligation; 'must', 'have to'.
source_long_explanation: The ～なきゃいけない grammar point is used to express a sense of necessity or obligation, similar to saying 'must' or 'have to' in English. It is a casual and more colloquial form of the ～なければいけない grammar point. The formation is different for verbs, but it is not used with い-adjectives, な-adjectives, or nouns.
source_formation: Verb-casual (negative form without い) + なきゃいけない

source_examples.japanese: 明日までに宿題を終わらなきゃいけない。
source_examples.translation_en: I have to finish my homework by tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: もうすぐ出かけるから、急いで準備しなきゃいけない。
source_examples.translation_en: We're leaving soon, so I have to hurry and get ready.

source_examples.japanese: このプロジェクトは来週提出しなきゃいけない。
source_examples.translation_en: I must submit this project by next week.

source_examples.japanese: 電車に乗る前に、切符を買わなきゃいけない。
source_examples.translation_en: I have to buy a ticket before getting on the train.

source_title: ～なくちゃいけない (〜naku cha ikenai)
source_short_explanation: Express the obligation to do something; 'have to', 'must', 'need to'.
source_long_explanation: The ～なくちゃいけない grammar point is used to express that there is an obligation or necessity to do something. It can be translated as 'have to', 'must', or 'need to' in English. This grammar point is mainly used with verbs.
source_formation: Verb-ない form (-ない ending is dropped) + なくちゃいけない

source_examples.japanese: 仕事に行かなくちゃいけないので、早起きしなければなりません。
source_examples.translation_en: I have to go to work, so I must wake up early.

source_examples.japanese: 試験があるから、勉強しなくちゃいけません。
source_examples.translation_en: I have a test, so I must study.

source_examples.japanese: パスポートを更新しなくちゃいけないので、大使館に行かなければ。
source_examples.translation_en: I have to renew my passport, so I need to go to the embassy.

source_examples.japanese: 今日はお金を払わなくちゃいけないから、銀行に行かないと。
source_examples.translation_en: I have to pay money today, so I need to go to the bank.

source_title: ～なくてはいけない (〜nakute wa ikenai)
source_short_explanation: Expresses the necessity or obligation; 'must', 'have to'.
source_long_explanation: The ～なくてはいけない grammar point is used to express the necessity or obligation to do something. It can be translated as 'must' or 'have to' in English. The formation requires the negative form of a verb and is followed by いけない (cannot go/progress). It indicates that if something is not done, it will be a problem or inappropriate.
source_formation: Verb-negative form + なくてはいけない

source_examples.japanese: 宿題をしなくてはいけない。
source_examples.translation_en: I have to do my homework.

source_examples.japanese: この手紙を明日までに出さなくてはいけない。
source_examples.translation_en: I must send this letter by tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: 食べ物を無駄にしなくてはいけない。
source_examples.translation_en: We must not waste food.

source_examples.japanese: 早退したいが、授業が終わるまで待たなくてはいけない。
source_examples.translation_en: I want to leave early, but I have to wait until the class finishes.

source_short_explanation: Expresses that something is not necessary to do; 'it's okay if not', 'don't have to'.
source_long_explanation: The ～なくてもいい grammar point is used to express that an action or situation is not necessary or required, implying that it's okay if it does not occur. It can be translated as 'it's okay if not' or 'don't have to' in English. This grammar is used with verbs.
source_formation: Verb-ない-form + てもいい

source_examples.japanese: コーヒーは飲まなくてもいいです。
source_examples.translation_en: You don't have to drink the coffee.

source_examples.japanese: 宿題を今日しなくてもいいです。
source_examples.translation_en: It's okay if you don't do your homework today.

source_examples.japanese: すぐに返事をしなくてもいいですよ。
source_examples.translation_en: You don't have to reply immediately.

source_examples.japanese: 全部食べなくてもいいですから、無理しないでください。
source_examples.translation_en: You don't have to eat everything, so please don't force yourself.

source_title: ～なければ ならない (〜nakereba naranai)
source_short_explanation: Express obligation or necessity; 'must', 'have to', 'need to'.
source_long_explanation: The ～なければ ならない grammar point is used to express obligation or necessity. In English, it can be translated as 'must', 'have to', or 'need to'. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb. It cannot be used with い-adjectives, な-adjectives or nouns.
source_formation: Verb-ない form + なければ ならない

source_examples.japanese: 宿題をやらなければならない。
source_examples.translation_en: I have to do my homework.

source_examples.japanese: 明日までにこの本を読まなければならない。
source_examples.translation_en: I have to read this book by tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: 授業に遅れないように、早く起きなければならない。
source_examples.translation_en: I have to wake up early so I don't be late for class.

source_examples.japanese: 旅行に行く前に切符を買わなければならない。
source_examples.translation_en: I have to buy a ticket before going on a trip.

source_short_explanation: Indicates direction, destination, purpose, or time.
source_long_explanation: The ～に grammar point is one of the most versatile Japanese particles. It is commonly used to indicate the direction or destination of an action, to show the purpose of an action or item, or to specify a point in time. Depending on the context, it can be translated as 'to', 'at', 'in', 'on', or 'for' in English.
source_formation: Noun + に

source_examples.japanese: 母は私にケーキを作りました。
source_examples.translation_en: My mother made a cake for me.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は東京に引っ越しました。
source_examples.translation_en: She moved to Tokyo.

source_examples.japanese: 銀行にお金を預けます。
source_examples.translation_en: I deposit money in the bank.

source_examples.japanese: 私は７時に起きます。
source_examples.translation_en: I wake up at 7 o'clock.

source_short_explanation: Express a reason or a cause for something; 'because', 'since', 'so'.
source_long_explanation: The ～ので grammar point is used to express reason or cause for something. It can be translated as 'because', 'since', or 'so' in English. It is similar to から but is considered more polite and formal. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
source_formation: Verb-casual + ので, い-Adjective + ので, な-Adjective + なので, Noun + なので

source_examples.japanese: 明日試験があるので、今晩勉強します。
source_examples.translation_en: I will study tonight because there is a test tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: このドレスが高いので、買わないことにします。
source_examples.translation_en: I will not buy this dress because it is expensive.

source_examples.japanese: 田中さんは病気なので、今日は来ません。
source_examples.translation_en: Tanaka-san will not come today since he is sick.

source_examples.japanese: 雨が降っているので、外に出ない方がいいですよ。
source_examples.translation_en: It is better not to go outside because it is raining.

source_short_explanation: Provides an explanation or gives background information; 'the fact is', 'the reason is', 'actually'.
source_long_explanation: The ～のです grammar point is used to provide an explanation or give background information on a situation, often used when there is a need to justify or clarify one's statement. It can be translated as 'the fact is', 'the reason is', or 'actually' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
source_formation: Verb-casual + のです, い-Adjective + のです, な-Adjective + なのです, Noun + なのです

source_examples.japanese: この本は難しいのです。
source_examples.translation_en: This book is difficult, you see.

source_examples.japanese: 明日は忙しいのです。
source_examples.translation_en: The fact is, I am busy tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は英語の先生なのです。
source_examples.translation_en: The reason is, she is an English teacher.

source_examples.japanese: 私は風邪なのです。
source_examples.translation_en: Actually, I’ve got a cold.

source_short_explanation: Used to express contrast between expectation and reality, or to indicate a purpose for doing something
source_long_explanation: The ～のに grammar point has two main usages. The first is to express contrast between an expectation and reality, with translations like 'even though', 'despite' or 'in spite of' in English. The second is to indicate a purpose for doing something, translated as 'in order to' or 'for the purpose of'. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
source_formation: Verb-casual + のに, い-Adjective + のに, な-Adjective + なのに, Noun + なのに

source_examples.japanese: 遅刻したのに、先生は怒らなかった。
source_examples.translation_en: Even though I was late, the teacher didn't get angry.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は疲れているのに、まだ働いています。
source_examples.translation_en: Despite being tired, he is still working.

source_examples.japanese: 勉強するのに静かな場所が必要です。
source_examples.translation_en: In order to study, I need a quiet place.

source_examples.japanese: 健康のために毎日運動するのに、うちでヨガをしている。
source_examples.translation_en: In order to exercise for my health every day, I do yoga at home.

source_short_explanation: Express a suggestion or advice; 'should', 'it would be good if'.
source_long_explanation: The ～ばいい grammar point is used to express a suggestion, recommendation or advice. It can be translated as 'should', or 'it would be good if' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
source_formation: Verb-ば-form + いい, い-Adjective + ければいい, な-Adjective + であればいい, Noun + であればいい

source_examples.japanese: もっと勉強すればいい。
source_examples.translation_en: You should study more.

source_examples.japanese: お腹が空いたら、何か食べればいい。
source_examples.translation_en: If you're hungry, you should eat something.

source_examples.japanese: もっと速く走ればいい。
source_examples.translation_en: You should run faster.

source_examples.japanese: わからなければ、先生に聞けばいい。
source_examples.translation_en: If you don't understand, you should ask the teacher.

source_short_explanation: Indicates extent, 'until', 'up to', 'as far as', 'even'.
source_long_explanation: The ～まで grammar point is used to express extent or range in terms of time, distance, or degree. It can be translated as 'until', 'up to', 'as far as', or 'even' in English. It is used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, or nouns.
source_formation: Verb + まで, い-Adjective + まで, な-Adjective + まで, Noun + まで

source_examples.japanese: 仕事が終わるまで待っています。
source_examples.translation_en: I will wait until work is finished.

source_examples.japanese: ここから駅まで歩いて10分かかります。
source_examples.translation_en: It takes 10 minutes to walk from here to the station.

source_examples.japanese: 私は彼が成功するまで応援します。
source_examples.translation_en: I will support him until he succeeds.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は猫まで好きです。
source_examples.translation_en: She likes even cats.

source_short_explanation: Express 'by' or 'before' a certain time or action.
source_long_explanation: The ～までに grammar point is used to indicate that something must be completed or occurs by a certain time or before a specific action. It can be used with verbs, nouns, and time expressions.
source_formation: Verb-casual + までに, Noun + までに, Time expression + までに

source_examples.japanese: 明日の朝８時までに起きてください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please wake up by 8 a.m. tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: 来週の金曜日までにレポートを提出してください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please submit the report by next Friday.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が帰るまでに料理を終わらせたい。
source_examples.translation_en: I want to finish cooking before he comes back.

source_examples.japanese: ３０分までに駅に着く必要があります。
source_examples.translation_en: We need to arrive at the station by 30 minutes (from now).

source_short_explanation: Express 'as it is', 'while' or 'unchanged state'.
source_long_explanation: The ～まま grammar point is used to express a state or condition that remains unchanged or continues, often translated as 'as it is', 'while', or 'unchanged'. It can be used with verbs and adjectives to show that something remains in a certain state or condition.
source_formation: Verb-てform + いる+ まま, Adjective (い & な) + まま, Noun + のまま

source_examples.japanese: ドアを開けたまま出かけてしまった。
source_examples.translation_en: I accidentally left with the door open.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は目覚まし時計を止めたまま寝てしまった。
source_examples.translation_en: He fell asleep with the alarm clock stopped.

source_examples.japanese: その部屋はきれいなままにしておいてください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please keep the room clean.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は子供のままの心を持っている。
source_examples.translation_en: She has the heart of a child.

source_short_explanation: Indicates similarity, resemblance or 'like'; 'it seems', 'appears', 'looks like'.
source_long_explanation: The ～みたいだ grammar point is used to express that something appears, seems or resembles something else. It can be used with nouns, verbs, い-adjectives, and な-adjectives. It can be translated as 'it seems', 'appears', or 'looks like' in English.
source_formation: Verb-casual + みたいだ, い-Adjective + みたいだ, な-Adjective + みたいだ, Noun + みたいだ

source_examples.japanese: 彼女が病気のみたいだ。
source_examples.translation_en: She seems to be sick.

source_examples.japanese: このドレスは高いみたいだ。
source_examples.translation_en: This dress seems to be expensive.

source_examples.japanese: あの人は有名人みたいだ。
source_examples.translation_en: That person looks like a celebrity.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は今忙しいみたいだ。
source_examples.translation_en: It seems he is busy right now.

source_short_explanation: Indicates 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.
source_long_explanation: The ～も grammar point is used to express that something is also true, or to add some additional information to the previous statement. It can be translated as 'also', 'too', or 'as well' in English. The grammar point can be used with verbs, adjectives, and nouns.
source_formation: Verb-casual + も, い-Adjective + も, な-Adjective + も, Noun + も

source_examples.japanese: 私もお寿司が好きです。
source_examples.translation_en: I also like sushi.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は英語も日本語も話せます。
source_examples.translation_en: She can speak both English and Japanese.

source_examples.japanese: その映画は面白いし、彼も見たいと言っています。
source_examples.translation_en: That movie is interesting, and he also said he wants to see it.

source_examples.japanese: 今日は寒いです。明日も寒いでしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: It is cold today. It will probably be cold tomorrow as well.

source_short_explanation: Expresses appearance, similarity or inference; 'it seems', 'it looks like', 'it appears'.
source_long_explanation: The ～ようだ grammar point is used to express appearance, similarity or inference about a situation or action. It can be translated as 'it seems', 'it looks like', or 'it appears' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
source_formation: Verb-て form + ようだ, い-Adjective (drop い) + ようだ, な-Adjective + のようだ, Noun + のようだ

source_examples.japanese: 彼は元気がないようだ。
source_examples.translation_en: He seems to be lacking energy.

source_examples.japanese: この料理は美味しいようだ。
source_examples.translation_en: This dish seems to be delicious.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は有名人のようだ。
source_examples.translation_en: She seems like a famous person.

source_examples.japanese: この部屋は図書館のようだ。
source_examples.translation_en: This room looks like a library.

source_short_explanation: Provide an explanation or reason; 'it is that', 'the thing is', 'the reason is'.
source_long_explanation: The ～んです grammar point is used to provide an explanation or reason for a situation or action. It can be translated as 'it is that', 'the thing is', or 'the reason is' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
source_formation: Verb-casual + んです, い-Adjective + んです, な-Adjective + なんです, Noun + なんです

source_examples.japanese: 遅れたんですが、電車が遅れました。
source_examples.translation_en: I was late because the train was delayed.

source_examples.japanese: 疲れたんです。
source_examples.translation_en: I'm tired (that's why).

source_examples.japanese: 彼は優しいんです。
source_examples.translation_en: The thing is, he is kind.

source_examples.japanese: 宿題が多いんです。
source_examples.translation_en: The reason is I have a lot of homework.

source_short_explanation: Shows additional information; 'furthermore', 'besides', 'in addition'.
source_long_explanation: This grammar point is used to connect two sentences, where the first sentence 文A provides some information, and the second sentence 文B adds additional related information. It can be translated as 'furthermore', 'besides', or 'in addition' in English.
source_formation: Sentence A + そのうえ + Sentence B + 。

source_examples.japanese: このソフトウェアは使いやすい。そのうえ、価格も手ごろだ。
source_examples.translation_en: This software is easy to use. Furthermore, the price is reasonable.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は美人だ。そのうえ、頭もいい。
source_examples.translation_en: She is beautiful. In addition, she is smart.

source_examples.japanese: この映画は面白い。そのうえ、俳優たちの演技も素晴らしい。
source_examples.translation_en: This movie is interesting. Besides, the actors' performances are also great.

source_examples.japanese: 東京はたくさんの観光スポットがある。そのうえ、美味しいレストランも多い。
source_examples.translation_en: Tokyo has many sightseeing spots. In addition, there are many delicious restaurants.

source_title: 文A。それで 文B (Bun A. Sorede Bun B)
source_short_explanation: Used to connect two sentences; 'So', 'That's why', 'Therefore'.
source_long_explanation: The grammar point 文A。それで 文B is used to connect two sentences and show that the second sentence (文B) is a result or consequence of the first sentence (文A). It can be translated as 'so', 'that's why', or 'therefore' in English.
source_formation: Sentence A。それで Sentence B。

source_examples.japanese: 今日は暑いです。それで、エアコンをつけました。
source_examples.translation_en: It is hot today. So, I turned on the air conditioner.

source_examples.japanese: 電車が遅れました。それで、仕事に遅れてしまいました。
source_examples.translation_en: The train was delayed. That's why I was late for work.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は疲れている。それで、早く寝ることにした。
source_examples.translation_en: He is tired. Therefore, he decided to go to bed early.

source_examples.japanese: 試験に合格しました。それで、友達とお祝いパーティーを開きました。
source_examples.translation_en: I passed the exam. So, I held a celebration party with friends.

source_title: 文A。それに 文B (Bun A. Soreni Bun B)
source_short_explanation: Express 'in addition to; besides,' used to include additional information.
source_long_explanation: This grammar point 文A。それに 文B is used to express an additional statement on what was mentioned earlier. It can be translated as 'in addition to,' 'besides,' or 'on top of that,' in English. It connects two sentences by highlighting supplementary information, opinions, or reasons.
source_formation: Sentence A + それに + Sentence B

source_examples.japanese: 彼は頭がいい。それに、スポーツも得意だ。
source_examples.translation_en: He is smart. In addition, he is good at sports.

source_examples.japanese: このケーキはおいしい。それに、値段も安い。
source_examples.translation_en: This cake is delicious. Besides, the price is also cheap.

source_examples.japanese: 私は日本語が話せます。それに、韓国語も話せます。
source_examples.translation_en: I can speak Japanese. On top of that, I can also speak Korean.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は美人だ。それに、性格もいい。
source_examples.translation_en: She is beautiful. In addition, she has a good personality.

source_title: 文A。だから 文B (Bun A. Dakara Bun B)
source_short_explanation: Express reason or cause; 'because', 'so', 'therefore'.
source_long_explanation: The 文A。だから 文B grammar point is used to indicate that the reason or cause of an action or event expressed in the second sentence (文B) is a result or consequence of the situation described in the first sentence (文A). It can be translated as 'because', 'so', or 'therefore' in English.
source_formation: Sentence A + だから + Sentence B

source_examples.japanese: 明日は試験だ。だから今日勉強しなければならない。
source_examples.translation_en: Tomorrow is the exam, so I have to study today.

source_examples.japanese: この料理は簡単だ。だから初心者でも作れる。
source_examples.translation_en: This dish is simple, so even beginners can make it.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は病気だ。だから今日学校を休む。
source_examples.translation_en: He is sick, so he will take a day off from school today.

source_examples.japanese: 駅まで遠い。だからタクシーで行ったほうがいい。
source_examples.translation_en: The station is far, so it's better to go by taxi.

source_title: A その上 B (A sono ue B)
source_short_explanation: Used to express 'in addition to', 'besides', or 'furthermore' when adding information or making a suggestion.
source_long_explanation: The grammar point A その上 B is used to connect two statements, where B is an additional piece of information, a suggestion or reason that is related to statement A. The expression can be translated as 'in addition to', 'besides', or 'furthermore'.
source_formation: A [sentence/clause] + その上 + B [sentence/clause]

source_examples.japanese: 彼は頭が良い。その上、スポーツも得意だ。
source_examples.translation_en: He is smart. In addition, he is also good at sports.

source_examples.japanese: このカフェは雰囲気がいい。その上、料理も美味しい。
source_examples.translation_en: This cafe has a nice atmosphere. Besides, the food is delicious.

source_examples.japanese: このアパートは駅に近い。その上、家賃も安い。
source_examples.translation_en: This apartment is close to the station. Furthermore, the rent is also cheap.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は仕事ができる。その上、誰とでも仲良くなれる。
source_examples.translation_en: She is competent at work. In addition, she can get along with anyone.

source_short_explanation: Express 'while', 'before', or 'during' a certain condition or situation.
source_long_explanation: The ～うちに grammar point is used to express the idea of doing something while a certain condition or situation is still present or before it changes. It can be translated as 'while', 'before', or 'during' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, or な-adjective.
source_formation: Verb-てform + いる + うちに, い-Adjective + い + うちに, な-Adjective + な + うちに

source_examples.japanese: 若いうちに、いろいろな経験をしておくことが大切です。
source_examples.translation_en: It is important to have various experiences while you are young.

source_examples.japanese: 雨が降っていないうちに、買い物に行こう。
source_examples.translation_en: Let's go shopping before it starts raining.

source_examples.japanese: 料理が熱いうちに食べましょう。
source_examples.translation_en: Let's eat while the food is still hot.

source_examples.japanese: 休みのうちに、旅行の計画を立てたいです。
source_examples.translation_en: I want to plan a trip during the holidays.

source_short_explanation: Express an action someone tried to do but couldn't; 'tried to', 'attempted to'.
source_long_explanation: The ～うとした grammar point is used to express an action that someone tried to do but couldn't complete, for various reasons. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with verbs. This grammar point can be translated as 'tried to' or 'attempted to' in English.
source_formation: Verb-う stem + とした

source_examples.japanese: 電話に出ようとしたが、相手は切ってしまった。
source_examples.translation_en: I tried to answer the phone, but the other person hung up.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は大声で話そうとしたが、言葉が出なかった。
source_examples.translation_en: He tried to speak loudly, but no words came out.

source_examples.japanese: ケーキを作ろうとしたが、材料が足りなかった。
source_examples.translation_en: I tried to make a cake, but I didn't have enough ingredients.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は泳ごうとしたが、怖くて水に入れなかった。
source_examples.translation_en: She tried to swim, but she was scared and couldn't get in the water.

source_short_explanation: Expresses gratitude or shows a positive result due to a certain factor; 'thanks to', 'because of'.
source_long_explanation: The ～おかげで grammar point is used to express gratitude or show a positive outcome resulting from a certain factor, event or person. It can be translated as 'thanks to' or 'because of' in English. The formation is straightforward and can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
source_formation: Verb-casual + おかげで, い-Adjective + おかげで, な-Adjective + だおかげで, Noun + のおかげで

source_examples.japanese: お母さんのおかげで、私は元気になりました。
source_examples.translation_en: Thanks to my mother, I became healthy.

source_examples.japanese: 先生の助けのおかげで、試験に合格しました。
source_examples.translation_en: Thanks to the teacher's help, I passed the exam.

source_examples.japanese: 日本語の勉強のおかげで、この映画が理解できました。
source_examples.translation_en: Thanks to studying Japanese, I was able to understand this movie.

source_examples.japanese: 晴れた天気のおかげで、ピクニックが楽しかったです。
source_examples.translation_en: Thanks to the sunny weather, the picnic was enjoyable.

source_short_explanation: Expresses the meaning of being in the middle of doing something or of something being partway done.
source_long_explanation: The ～かけ grammar point is used to indicate that something is in the process of being done or is partway completed. This is often used with verbs to describe an action that is not yet finished or is ongoing. The verb should be in its ます-form, and かけ is added after removing the ます.
source_formation: Verb-ますstem + かけ

source_examples.japanese: 彼は食事を食べかけです。
source_examples.translation_en: He is in the middle of eating his meal.

source_examples.japanese: この本は読みかけで、まだ終わっていません。
source_examples.translation_en: This book is partway read, and it is not yet finished.

source_examples.japanese: この部屋は掃除しかけで、まだ片づいていません。
source_examples.translation_en: This room is partway cleaned, and it's not yet tidied up.

source_examples.japanese: プロジェクトは進行しかけで、来週には完了する予定です。
source_examples.translation_en: The project is in progress and is scheduled to be completed next week.

source_short_explanation: Express 'without doing ~' or 'without ~ing'.
source_long_explanation: The ～ないで grammar point is used to express the idea of 'without doing something' or 'without ~ing' in English. It is formed by attaching the ない-form of the verb and adding で (de). This is used for expressing when an action is not taken or avoided, without interfering with the main action.
source_formation: Verb-ない-form + で

source_examples.japanese: 会わないでその電話をかけました。
source_examples.translation_en: I made the phone call without meeting them.

source_examples.japanese: 雨が降るのを待たないで、家を出ました。
source_examples.translation_en: I left the house without waiting for it to rain.

source_examples.japanese: 誰にも聞かないで、その秘密を知りました。
source_examples.translation_en: I found out the secret without asking anyone.

source_examples.japanese: 遅れることを知らないで、駅に向かいました。
source_examples.translation_en: I headed to the station without knowing I was late.

source_short_explanation: Expresses a range of something, such as time or space; 'from...to', 'between'.
source_long_explanation: The ～から～にかけて grammar point is used to show a range, whether it is a range of time, space, or another measure. It can be translated as 'from...to' or 'between' in English. This grammar point is commonly used with nouns indicating time or place.
source_formation: Noun (time, place, or measure) + から + Noun (time, place or measure) + にかけて

source_examples.japanese: 午前８時から午後５時にかけて働いています。
source_examples.translation_en: I work from 8 am to 5 pm.

source_examples.japanese: この地域は、北から南にかけて狭いです。
source_examples.translation_en: This area is narrow from north to south.

source_examples.japanese: １０歳から２０歳にかけて成長が早いです。
source_examples.translation_en: Growth is rapid from 10 to 20 years of age.

source_examples.japanese: 今年の夏は、６月から８月にかけて雨が多かった。
source_examples.translation_en: This summer, there was a lot of rain from June to August.

source_short_explanation: In place of; instead of; as a substitute for.
source_long_explanation: The ～かわりに grammar point is used to express doing something in place of or as a substitute for something else. It can be translated as 'instead of', 'in place of', or 'as a substitute for' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
source_formation: Verb-casual + かわりに, い-Adjective + かわりに, な-Adjective + だかわりに, Noun + だかわりに

source_examples.japanese: 映画を見るかわりに、本を読んだ。
source_examples.translation_en: Instead of watching a movie, I read a book.

source_examples.japanese: お酒を飲むかわりに、水を飲んでください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please drink water instead of alcohol.

source_examples.japanese: 犬のかわりに、猫を飼いたいです。
source_examples.translation_en: I want to keep a cat instead of a dog.

source_examples.japanese: 電車を使わないかわりに、自転車で行くことにしました。
source_examples.translation_en: I decided to go by bicycle instead of using the train.

source_short_explanation: Expresses the idea of 'only', 'since', or 'after'.
source_long_explanation: The ～きり grammar point is used to express the idea of 'only', 'since', or 'after'. It indicates that a certain action or state continues without any change since a specific point in time or after a certain event. It is commonly used with verbs in the past tense, but can also be used with other forms.
source_formation: Verb-past + きり, Verb-てform + きり (less common), Noun + きり

source_examples.japanese: 彼は出かけたきり帰ってきません。
source_examples.translation_en: He went out and hasn't come back since.

source_examples.japanese: 昨日コーヒーを飲んだきり、何も飲まなかった。
source_examples.translation_en: I haven't had anything to drink since the coffee I had yesterday.

source_examples.japanese: 卒業したきり、彼女に会っていません。
source_examples.translation_en: I haven't seen her since we graduated.

source_examples.japanese: その映画を見たきり、もう一度見たいと思っています。
source_examples.translation_en: I've wanted to watch that movie again ever since I saw it.

source_short_explanation: Used to express criticism or disapproval; 'even though', 'despite', 'in spite of'.
source_long_explanation: The ～くせに grammar point is used to express criticism or disapproval in a sentence. It can be translated as 'even though', 'despite', or 'in spite of' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
source_formation: Verb-casual + くせに, い-Adjective + くせに, な-Adjective + な/のくせに, Noun + のくせに

source_examples.japanese: 彼はお金持ちのくせに、ケチです。
source_examples.translation_en: Even though he's rich, he's stingy.

source_examples.japanese: この部屋が汚いくせに、文句を言うな。
source_examples.translation_en: Don't complain even though this room is dirty. (criticizing)

source_examples.japanese: 彼は暇なくせに、手伝ってくれません。
source_examples.translation_en: Even though he's free, he won't help me.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は美人なくせに、デートが続かない。
source_examples.translation_en: Even though she's beautiful, she can't keep a date going.

source_short_explanation: Expresses an approximate quantity or degree; 'about', 'approximately', or 'to the extent of'.
