source_examples.japanese: この難しい問題は解決しそうもない。
source_examples.translation_en: It doesn't seem like this difficult problem will be solved.

source_short_explanation: Expresses that as soon as one action finishes, another begins immediately.
source_long_explanation: The 〜そばから grammar point is used to indicate that right after a certain action is completed, another action takes place—often suggesting a repetitive or frustrating cycle.
source_formation: Verb-ますstem + そばから

source_examples.japanese: 掃除をするそばから子供たちが散らかす。
source_examples.translation_en: As soon as I clean, the kids mess it up.

source_examples.japanese: 仕事を終えるそばから新たな仕事が舞い込んできた。
source_examples.translation_en: As soon as I finished my work, a new task came in.

source_examples.japanese: それを解決するそばからまた別の問題が出てきた。
source_examples.translation_en: As soon as we solve that, another problem arises.

source_examples.japanese: 眠りにつくそばから電話が鳴った。
source_examples.translation_en: The phone rang as soon as I fell asleep.

source_title: Verb たが最後 (〜ta ga saigo)
source_short_explanation: Emphasizes 'once something happens, there is no going back'; 'once', 'as soon as', etc.
source_long_explanation: The 〜たが最後 grammar point indicates that once an action is taken or event occurs, some (often irreversible) consequence follows. In English, it can be translated as 'once', 'as soon as', or 'the moment that...'.
source_formation: Verb-casual, past (た form) + が最後

source_examples.japanese: 彼が一度怒ったが最後、誰も彼を止めることはできません。
source_examples.translation_en: Once he gets angry, no one can stop him.

source_examples.japanese: このゲームを始めたが最後、一晩中やり続けた。
source_examples.translation_en: As soon as I started this game, I played it all night.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女が部屋を出たが最後、二度と戻ってこなかった。
source_examples.translation_en: The moment she left the room, she never came back.

source_examples.japanese: 私がその橋を渡ったが最後、それが最後の別れだった。
source_examples.translation_en: Once I crossed that bridge, it was our final goodbye.

pattern: Verbたことにしてください
source_title: Verb たことにしてください (~ ta koto ni shite kudasai)
source_short_explanation: Asking someone to pretend or accept that something has already happened or taken a certain state.
source_long_explanation: The grammar point 'Verb たことにしてください' is used to request someone to act as if or pretend that a certain action has already occurred or a certain state exists. It is used in various contexts to express the idea of accepting a hypothetical situation for convenience or to avoid conflicts.
source_formation: Verb (past, casual) + ことにしてください

source_examples.japanese: 昨日のことは忘れたことにしてください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please act as if you have forgotten about yesterday.

source_examples.japanese: 私がここに来たことを誰にも言わないで、秘密にしたことにしてください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please don't tell anyone that I came here; act as if it’s a secret.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が間違えたと思ったことにしてください。
source_examples.translation_en: Please pretend that you think he made a mistake.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女が帰ったことにしてください。
source_examples.translation_en: Let’s pretend that she has gone home.

source_title: Verb たら Verb たで (~ tara ~ tade)
source_short_explanation: Conveys that if something happens (or doesn’t happen), there is a particular consequence or situation either way.
source_long_explanation: The pattern VerbたらVerbたで is used for scenarios where doing something creates a certain issue or reaction, and not doing it also creates a different concern. It often shows that no matter which side of the condition you end up on, there’s some related result or trouble.
source_formation: Verb-た form + ら + (same Verb-た form) + で

source_examples.japanese: 行ったら行ったで大変だし、行かなかったら行かなかったで後悔しそうだ。
source_examples.translation_en: If I go, it’s a hassle; if I don’t go, I’ll regret it.

source_examples.japanese: 買ったら買ったでお金がなくなるし、買わなかったら買わなかったで後で欲しくなる。
source_examples.translation_en: If I buy it, I’ll run out of money; if I don’t buy it, I’ll want it later.

source_examples.japanese: 作ったら作ったで食べきれないし、作らなかったら作らなかったでお腹が空く。
source_examples.translation_en: If I cook, I can’t finish it all; if I don’t, I’ll be hungry.

source_examples.japanese: 旅行に出かけたら出かけたで疲れるし、家にいたらいたで退屈する。
source_examples.translation_en: If I go on a trip, I'll get tired, but if I stay home, I'll be bored.

source_title: Verb たら きりがない (Verb tara kiri ga nai)
source_short_explanation: Indicates an endless or unending cycle once an action is started; 'if one starts doing something, it will not stop.'
source_long_explanation: The たらきりがない grammar pattern is used when something negative or undesirable continues indefinitely once it begins. The implication is that you should avoid initiating the action because it’ll just go on and on.
source_formation: Verb-た form + ら + きりがない

source_examples.japanese: このエンジンを修理したら、またすぐ壊れて、直したらきりがない。
source_examples.translation_en: If I fix this engine, it breaks again, and if I fix it again, it never ends.

source_examples.japanese: 飲み始めたらきりがない。
source_examples.translation_en: Once I start drinking, I never stop.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女にお金を貸したら、きりがない。
source_examples.translation_en: If I lend her money, there will be no end to it.

source_examples.japanese: 彼の話を聞き始めたらきりがない。
source_examples.translation_en: Once you start listening to his stories, it never ends.

source_short_explanation: Expresses that once a certain action happens, the situation changes irreversibly—usually in a negative way.
source_long_explanation: The たら最後 grammar point indicates that once an action (in た-form) occurs, there is no going back and an unpleasant or unavoidable state follows. Often translated as 'once...then it's all over' or 'the moment...there’s no turning back.'
source_formation: Verb-た form + ら最後

source_examples.japanese: このゲームを始めたら最後、時間の経つのを忘れてしまいます。
source_examples.translation_en: Once you start this game, you completely lose track of time.

source_examples.japanese: 彼はビールを一杯飲み始めたら最後、止まらなくなります。
source_examples.translation_en: Once he starts drinking a beer, he can't stop.

source_examples.japanese: この本を読み始めたら最後、一気に読破してしまいました。
source_examples.translation_en: Once I started reading this book, I ended up finishing it in one go.

source_examples.japanese: 彼を怒らせたら最後、なかなか許してもらえないよ。
source_examples.translation_en: Once you make him angry, he won't forgive you so easily.

source_title: Verb つ Verb つ (Verb tsu Verb tsu)
source_short_explanation: Expresses two alternating actions happening repeatedly.
source_long_explanation: The 〜つ〜つ pattern is used with two verb ます-stems to express two ongoing, repeated or alternating actions. For example, 'push and pull,' 'go and come back,' 'eat and play,' etc. The same subject is typically implied for both verbs.
source_formation: Verb-ますstem + つ + Verb-ますstem + つ

source_examples.japanese: 朝から晩まで働きつ勉強しつで、疲れてしまった。
source_examples.translation_en: I’ve been working and studying from morning till night, and now I’m exhausted.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は話しつ笑いつして楽しんでいた。
source_examples.translation_en: He was talking and laughing, having a good time.

source_examples.japanese: 子供たちは食べつ遊びつしていた。
source_examples.translation_en: The children were eating and playing.

source_examples.japanese: 私は読みつ書きつして過ごした。
source_examples.translation_en: I spent my time reading and writing.

source_title: Verb てからというもの (Verb te kara to iu mono)
source_short_explanation: Expresses that ever since a certain event happened, a condition has continued until now.
source_long_explanation: The てからというもの grammar point indicates that from the time a certain action happened, a significant change or condition has persisted continuously. It emphasizes that the new situation contrasts with what came before.
source_formation: Verb-て form + からというもの

source_examples.japanese: 彼女と別れてからというもの、一人で過ごす時間が増えました。
source_examples.translation_en: Ever since I broke up with her, I've spent more time alone.

source_examples.japanese: 子供が生まれてからというもの、自由な時間がなくなった。
source_examples.translation_en: Since the baby was born, I have had no free time.

source_examples.japanese: 新しい仕事を始めてからというもの、毎日忙しくなりました。
source_examples.translation_en: Ever since I started my new job, I've been busy every day.

source_examples.japanese: 大学に入ってからというもの、スポーツをする時間がなくなった。
source_examples.translation_en: I haven’t had time to play sports since I entered university.

source_short_explanation: Emphasizes 'only by doing something, a certain result or realization can occur.'
source_long_explanation: The ～てこそ grammar point is used to highlight that only by performing the verb in て-form can a certain important outcome be achieved or recognized. It often translates as 'only by (doing)' or 'only when (doing).'
source_formation: Verb-て form + こそ

source_examples.japanese: 実際に使ってこそ、その価値を理解できる。
source_examples.translation_en: You can only understand its value by actually using it.

source_examples.japanese: 自分で経験してこそ、大切なことが学べる。
source_examples.translation_en: Only by experiencing it yourself can you learn what’s truly important.

source_examples.japanese: 失敗してこそ、成功の味がわかる。
source_examples.translation_en: Only by failing do you really understand the taste of success.

source_examples.japanese: 努力してこそ、何かを成し遂げることができる。
source_examples.translation_en: Only through making an effort can you accomplish anything.

source_short_explanation: Expresses a repeated pattern or cycle, often implying a frustrating outcome; 'whenever X happens, Y happens again.'
source_long_explanation: The grammar ～ては is used to show that whenever one action or situation occurs, another action or situation repeatedly follows. It can also be used in an alternating pattern: 'do this, then that, then this, then that.'
source_formation: Verb-て form + は

source_examples.japanese: 彼女に会っては、いつも緊張してしまいます。
source_examples.translation_en: Whenever I meet her, I get nervous.

source_examples.japanese: この部屋を掃除しては乱雑になり、片づけては散らかる。
source_examples.translation_en: Whenever I clean this room, it gets messy again, and whenever I tidy it, it gets cluttered again.

source_examples.japanese: 運動しては食べ、食べては運動する生活が続いている。
source_examples.translation_en: I keep exercising and then eating, and then eating and exercising.

source_examples.japanese: 勉強しては寝て、寝ては勉強する日々です。
source_examples.translation_en: My days are spent studying and then sleeping, and then sleeping and studying.

source_title: Verb ては Verb (~ te wa ~)
source_short_explanation: Expresses a repeated pattern of action; translates as 'every time', 'whenever', etc.
source_long_explanation: This grammar point is used when you want to express a repeated or cyclical pattern of actions or events. It can be translated as 'every time', 'whenever', or 'if at all'. The typical formation is a verb in the て-form, followed by は, and then another verb (often in the same tense or a continuing action).
source_formation: Verb-て form + は + Verb

source_examples.japanese: 私が通勤しては、電子書籍を読んでいます。
source_examples.translation_en: Whenever I commute, I read e-books.

source_examples.japanese: 友達が部屋に来ては、ゲームをしています。
source_examples.translation_en: Every time my friend comes to my room, we play games.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が酒を飲んでは、運転を止めさせています。
source_examples.translation_en: Whenever he drinks alcohol, I make him stop driving.

source_examples.japanese: 私が新しい曲を作っては、すぐに録音します。
source_examples.translation_en: Every time I create a new song, I record it immediately.

source_short_explanation: Expresses 'even if it means doing...', 'no matter what it takes'.
source_long_explanation: This grammar point is used when the speaker wants to emphasize the lengths they would go to in order to achieve something. It attaches to the verb's て-form to mean 'even if it means doing X', 'even at the cost of X', or 'no matter what it takes'.
source_formation: Verb-て form + までも

source_examples.japanese: 試験に合格するために、寝る時間を削ってまでも勉強します。
source_examples.translation_en: I will study to pass the exam, even if it means cutting down on sleep.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女と結婚できるなら、どんな苦労をしてまでもお金を貯めたい。
source_examples.translation_en: If I can marry her, I'll save money no matter what hardships it takes.

source_examples.japanese: この会社で働きたいので、長時間かけてまでも通います。
source_examples.translation_en: Because I want to work at this company, I'll commute even if it means spending hours traveling.

source_examples.japanese: 彼の快復のためなら、何をしてまでも支えたい。
source_examples.translation_en: For his recovery, I'll support him no matter what it takes.

source_title: Verb てみせる (Verb te miseru)
source_short_explanation: 'Show by doing', 'demonstrate', 'prove by action'.
source_long_explanation: The ～てみせる grammar point is used to express the action of demonstrating or proving something by actually doing it. It can be translated as 'show by doing', 'demonstrate', or 'prove by action' in English.
source_formation: Verb-て form + みせる

source_examples.japanese: 彼はそのパズルを解いてみせた。
source_examples.translation_en: He solved the puzzle to show me.

source_examples.japanese: 私はこの仕事ができることをやってみせます。
source_examples.translation_en: I will do this job to prove that I can.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は試験に合格するために一生懸命勉強してみせました。
source_examples.translation_en: She studied hard to prove she could pass the exam.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は自分が何も恐れていないと跳んでみせた。
source_examples.translation_en: He jumped to show he wasn’t afraid of anything.

source_title: Verb てやまない (Verb te yamanai)
source_short_explanation: Used with certain emotional/mental verbs to show a strong, unceasing emotion: 'can't stop', 'never cease to'.
source_long_explanation: The grammar ～てやまない is typically used with verbs like 願う, 祈る, 愛する, 尊敬する, 期待する, etc., expressing a deep, continuous emotional state (love, respect, hope, prayer). It emphasizes that the feeling 'never ceases.'
source_formation: Verb-て form + やまない (common with certain verbs)

source_examples.japanese: 私は母を思ってやまない。
source_examples.translation_en: I can't stop thinking of my mother.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は彼女を愛してやまない。
source_examples.translation_en: He loves her beyond measure.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は日本の文化を尊敬してやまない。
source_examples.translation_en: He has unceasing respect for Japanese culture.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女の成功を願ってやまない。
source_examples.translation_en: I can’t stop hoping for her success.

source_title: Verb ないではおかない (~ nai de wa okanai)
source_short_explanation: Means 'cannot help but do', 'will definitely do', or 'is bound to happen'.
source_long_explanation: The pattern Verb ないではおかない indicates that something definitely occurs as a logical or emotional consequence. It can be translated as 'cannot not do', 'can’t help but do', or 'will inevitably do'. The verb is put in the negative form followed by ないではおかない.
source_formation: Verb-ない form + ではおかない

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は毎回遅刻をしては、先生に怒られないではおかない。
source_examples.translation_en: Every time she's late, she inevitably gets scolded by the teacher.

source_examples.japanese: 美味しいものがあれば、彼は食べないではおかない。
source_examples.translation_en: If there's delicious food, he can't help but eat it.

source_examples.japanese: この小説は感動的で、読めば涙を流さないではおかない。
source_examples.translation_en: This novel is so moving that you can't help but shed tears when you read it.

source_examples.japanese: 毎日練習しているから、試合では勝たないではおかないだろう。
source_examples.translation_en: He practices every day, so he's bound to win the match.

source_title: Verb ないではすまない (Verb nai dewa sumanai)
source_short_explanation: 'Cannot end without doing', 'must do'—an unavoidable moral or social necessity.
source_long_explanation: The grammar Verb ないではすまない expresses that something must be done (often for moral, social, or personal reasons) and cannot be left undone. It implies an obligation or inevitability, akin to 'I can't get away without doing it.'
source_formation: Verb-ない form + ではすまない

source_examples.japanese: 失敗をしたら、謝らないではすまない。
source_examples.translation_en: If you make a mistake, you have to apologize—there’s no way around it.

source_examples.japanese: この問題は重大なので、報告しないではすまない。
source_examples.translation_en: This issue is so serious that I must report it.

source_examples.japanese: この映画はとても感動的で、泣かないではすまない。
source_examples.translation_en: This movie is so moving that you can’t help but cry.

source_examples.japanese: 子供が間違えたら、教えないではすまない。
source_examples.translation_en: If a child makes a mistake, you must correct them—there’s no avoiding it.

source_title: Verb ないまでも (Verb nai made mo)
source_short_explanation: 'Even if not to the extent of...', 'although not completely...'.
source_long_explanation: The pattern ないまでも is used when acknowledging that something doesn’t reach a certain extreme, but at least some part or degree of it applies. Often translated as 'even if not entirely...' or 'though not as far as...'.
source_formation: Verb-ない form + までも

source_examples.japanese: 全てを理解しないまでも、基本的なことは分かってほしい。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if you don't understand everything, I'd like you at least to grasp the basics.

source_examples.japanese: 会えないまでも、電話で声を聞きたい。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if we can’t meet, I still want to hear your voice over the phone.

source_examples.japanese: 毎日は無理にしても、週に一度くらいはジョギングを続けたい。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if I can't do it every day, I want to at least keep jogging once a week.

source_examples.japanese: 全員に気に入られないまでも、誠実に向き合いたい。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if not everyone will like me, I still want to face them sincerely.

source_title: Verb ないものだろうか (Verb nai mono darou ka)
source_short_explanation: Expressing hope or wonder if something can be done: 'Isn't there a way...?', 'Can't we...?'
source_long_explanation: This grammar point is used when the speaker expresses the hope, wish, or wonder if an action could be possible. It creates the nuance of 'Isn't there some way...?' or 'Can't I/you/we...?' in English, often with the negative potential form.
source_formation: Verb-negative (often negative potential) + ものだろうか

source_examples.japanese: もっと時間があれば、ここに来られないものだろうか。
source_examples.translation_en: If I had more time, wouldn't it be possible to come here?

source_examples.japanese: 彼女にもっとよく説明すれば、理解できないものだろうか。
source_examples.translation_en: If I explain it better to her, wouldn't she understand?

source_examples.japanese: この問題を解決する方法はないものだろうか。
source_examples.translation_en: Isn't there a way to solve this problem?

source_examples.japanese: 自分の間違いを認められないものだろうか。
source_examples.translation_en: Can't I admit my own mistakes?

source_title: Verb ないものでもない (Verb nai mono demo nai)
source_short_explanation: Expresses the idea that it's not entirely impossible or non-existent: 'It's not that I don't...', 'It's not that there aren't...'
source_long_explanation: The grammar point Verbないものでもない is used to express that a situation is not completely impossible or nonexistent. Literally, it can be translated as 'it's not that there aren't...' or 'it's not that I never...'. It implies that some possibility or partial truth exists.
source_formation: Verb-negative form (ない form) + ものでもない

source_examples.japanese: 旅行に行きたいと思わないものでもない。
source_examples.translation_en: It's not that I never want to travel.

source_examples.japanese: 彼の言ったこと全部が間違いないものでもない。
source_examples.translation_en: It's not that everything he said is completely free from mistakes.

source_examples.japanese: その問題が解けないものでもない。
source_examples.translation_en: It's not that the problem can't be solved.

source_examples.japanese: 彼に会いたくないものでもない。
source_examples.translation_en: It's not that I don't want to see him.

source_title: Verb の ない Noun (~ no nai ~)
source_short_explanation: Used to modify a noun with a negative verb form; 'a Noun without (Verb)'.
source_long_explanation: VerbのないNoun modifies a noun by describing the absence of the verb's action. It indicates 'a Noun where the action does not happen' or 'a Noun without that action.'
source_formation: Verb in negative form + の + Noun

source_examples.japanese: 笑いのない人生は、つまらない。
source_examples.translation_en: A life without laughter is boring.

source_examples.japanese: 水のない場所には、人は住めない。
source_examples.translation_en: People cannot live in a place without water.

source_examples.japanese: 言葉のない世界は、想像するのが難しい。
source_examples.translation_en: It's hard to imagine a world without words.

source_examples.japanese: 愛のない結婚は、長続きしない。
source_examples.translation_en: A marriage without love will not last.

source_title: Verb ば きりがない (〜ba kiri ga nai)
source_short_explanation: Indicates there's no end once you start listing, doing, or saying something: 'If one starts to..., there will be no end.'
source_long_explanation: The pattern ～ばきりがない is used when expressing that if you start an action—like listing examples or complaining—there is no end. It literally means 'if (you) do X, there's no limit/end.'
source_formation: Verb-conditional form (ば) + きりがない

source_examples.japanese: 悪口を言い始めればきりがない。
source_examples.translation_en: Once I start speaking ill of someone, there's no end.

source_examples.japanese: 彼の欠点を数えればきりがない。
source_examples.translation_en: If I start counting his flaws, there will be no end.

source_examples.japanese: この国の美しい場所は、挙げればきりがない。
source_examples.translation_en: If I start listing this country's beautiful places, there's no end.

source_examples.japanese: ほかにも例を挙げればきりがない。
source_examples.translation_en: If I start giving more examples, there will be no end.

source_title: Verb もしないで (~ mo shinai de)
source_short_explanation: Means 'without even doing'.
source_long_explanation: This pattern is used to express that one has not done (or not even tried to do) some action before proceeding to do something else. It emphasizes doing something 'without even' doing the prior action.
source_formation: Verb (masu stem) + もしないで

source_examples.japanese: 調べもしないで、答えを書きました。
source_examples.translation_en: I wrote the answer without even investigating.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は試験を勉強もしないで、テストに合格した。
source_examples.translation_en: He passed the test without even studying.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女はその本を読みもしないで、レポートを書いた。
source_examples.translation_en: She wrote her report without even reading the book.

source_examples.japanese: 準備もしないで、プレゼンテーションを始めました。
source_examples.translation_en: He started the presentation without even preparing.

source_short_explanation: Expresses a strong denial or refusal: 'I would never...', 'No way I would...'.
source_long_explanation: This grammar adds a nuance of strong denial or dismissal of the idea that the speaker (or someone) would do the action. Formed by adding やしない to the verb's stem, it often appears in casual or spoken language.
source_formation: Verb (masu stem) + やしない

source_examples.japanese: こんな時に泣きやしない。
source_examples.translation_en: I would never cry at a time like this.

source_examples.japanese: 私が彼を助けやしない。
source_examples.translation_en: There's no way I'd help him.

source_examples.japanese: 彼がそんなことを言いやしない。
source_examples.translation_en: He would never say such a thing.

source_examples.japanese: 私がそんな高価なものを買いやしない。
source_examples.translation_en: There's no way I'd buy something so expensive.

source_title: Verb よう (~ you / ~ you ni)
source_short_explanation: Expresses 'the way/manner of doing something' or 'in order to / so that / try to'.
source_long_explanation: This usage of よう most commonly appears as 「Verb辞書形 + ように」. It can mean 'in order to do something', 'so that something happens', or 'in the way someone does something'. It is also used in expressions like ～ようにする (to make an effort to) or ～ように言う (to tell someone to do something).
source_formation: Verb (dictionary or negative form) + ように (する / etc.)

source_examples.japanese: この問題を解くように努力します。
source_examples.translation_en: I will try to solve this problem.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が言ったようにやりましょう。
source_examples.translation_en: Let's do it the way he said.

source_examples.japanese: 毎日走るようにしています。
source_examples.translation_en: I make it a point to run every day.

source_examples.japanese: 自分の心を大切にするように。
source_examples.translation_en: Try to take care of your own heart.

source_title: Verb ようか Verbるまいか (Verb you ka Verb ru mai ka)
source_short_explanation: Expresses indecision: 'Should I do it or not?'.
source_long_explanation: This grammar shows hesitation about whether to do something or not. The volitional form plus まい (negative volitional) suggests an internal debate about two opposite choices of the *same* verb.
source_formation: Verb-volitional form + か + Verb-volitional negative form (まい) + か

source_examples.japanese: 彼に話そうか話すまいか、本当に迷っている。
source_examples.translation_en: I'm really unsure whether to talk to him or not.

source_examples.japanese: 試験を受けようか受けまいか迷っています。
source_examples.translation_en: I'm wondering whether to take the exam or not.

source_examples.japanese: あの人に謝ろうか謝るまいか考えています。
source_examples.translation_en: I'm considering whether to apologize to that person or not.

source_examples.japanese: 進学しようかしまいか悩んでいる。
source_examples.translation_en: I'm worried about whether to continue my studies or not.

source_title: Verb ようが Verb るまいが (Verb you ga Verb ru mai ga)
source_short_explanation: Expresses 'whether or not', 'no matter if something happens or not'.
source_long_explanation: Verbようが Verbるまいが indicates that whatever happens—whether the action is done or not—the outcome remains unchanged or the speaker's stance remains the same.
source_formation: Verb-volitional form + が + Verb-negative volitional form + が

source_examples.japanese: 彼が来ようが来るまいが、パーティーは始まります。
source_examples.translation_en: Whether he comes or not, the party will start.

source_examples.japanese: 勉強しようがしまいが、テストの結果は変わらない。
source_examples.translation_en: Whether you study or not, the test results won't change.

source_examples.japanese: 雨が降ろうが降るまいが、ピクニックに行きます。
source_examples.translation_en: Whether it rains or not, we're going on a picnic.

source_examples.japanese: 暑かろうが寒かろうが、毎日ジョギングします。
source_examples.translation_en: Whether it's hot or cold, I jog every day.

source_title: Verb ようがない (〜you ga nai)
source_short_explanation: Expresses 'no way to do something,' 'impossible to do'.
source_long_explanation: 〜ようがない is used to say that there's no way or method to do something, even if you wanted to.
source_formation: Verb (masu stem) + ようがない

source_examples.japanese: 電車が混んでいて、動きようがない。
source_examples.translation_en: The train is so crowded that I can't move.

source_examples.japanese: 彼はとても早く走るので、追いつきようがない。
source_examples.translation_en: He runs so fast, there's no way I can catch up.

source_examples.japanese: 私には理解しようがない。
source_examples.translation_en: There's no way for me to understand it.

source_examples.japanese: どうやっても、これを直しようがない。
source_examples.translation_en: No matter what I try, there's no way to fix this.

source_title: Verb ようと Verbる まいと (Verb you to Verb ru mai to)
source_short_explanation: This structure indicates that regardless of whether one does (verb) or not, the outcome/attitude remains unchanged.
source_long_explanation: The expression 'Verb-volitional form + と + Verb-negative volitional (～まい) + と' means 'regardless of whether one does X or not, it doesn't change the situation'. It shows the speaker's firm stance or the unchanging nature of some outcome.
source_formation: Verb-volitional + と + Verb-negative volitional (～まい) + と

source_examples.japanese: あなたが来ようと来るまいと、パーティーは予定通りに始まります。
source_examples.translation_en: Whether you come or not, the party will start as scheduled.

source_examples.japanese: 彼があそこに行こうと行くまいと、私たちは止めることができません。
source_examples.translation_en: Whether he tries to go there or not, we can't stop him.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女が謝ろうと謝るまいと、事実は変わらない。
source_examples.translation_en: Whether she apologizes or not, the fact won't change.

source_examples.japanese: 試験を受けようと受けるまいと、親として私はあなたを支えます。
source_examples.translation_en: Whether you take the exam or not, I will support you as your parent.

source_title: Verb ようにも (〜you ni mo)
source_short_explanation: Used to express 'even though one wants to do something, one can't for some reason'.
source_long_explanation: The ～ようにも grammar point indicates that a person wants or tries to do something (volitional form), but for some reason cannot. Often, there's a second clause explaining what prevents the action.
source_formation: Verb-volitional form + にも + (reason/potential negative, etc.)

source_examples.japanese: もう少し速く走ろうにも、足が痛くて無理だ。
source_examples.translation_en: I'd like to run a bit faster, but I can’t because my leg hurts.

source_examples.japanese: 彼に話そうにも、彼は私を無視している。
source_examples.translation_en: I want to talk to him, but he's ignoring me.

source_examples.japanese: もっと勉強しようにも、時間がない。
source_examples.translation_en: I want to study more, but I have no time.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女に謝ろうにも、彼女はもう怒っている。
source_examples.translation_en: I would like to apologize to her, but she's already angry.

source_title: Verb ようにも Verb れない (〜you ni mo 〜renai)
source_short_explanation: Expresses the inability to do something even if one wants/tries.
source_long_explanation: This grammar shows that you want (or try) to do something (volitional form), but cannot due to some obstacle. Often it appears as 'Verb-volitional + にも + Verb (potential negative)' or simply 'Verb-volitional + にも + (reason you can't)'.
source_formation: Verb-volitional form + にも + (potential negative form / reason)

source_examples.japanese: 彼を信じようにも信じられない証拠がある。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if I want to believe him, there's evidence that prevents me from doing so.

source_examples.japanese: 早く出発しようにも車が故障してしまった。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if I want to leave early, my car has broken down.

source_examples.japanese: 彼に電話しようにも電話番号を知らない。
source_examples.translation_en: I want to call him, but I don’t know his phone number.

source_examples.japanese: もっと勉強しようにも時間がない。
source_examples.translation_en: I want to study more, but there is no time.

source_title: Verb ようもない (~you mo nai)
source_short_explanation: Expresses 'it's impossible to do something'.
source_long_explanation: ～ようもない typically attaches to the verb's ます-stem, adding ようもない to indicate that there is 'no way' or 'no method' to perform the action. It’s the same nuance as 'Verbようがない' in many references.
source_formation: Verb-ます stem + ようもない

source_examples.japanese: この問題は解きようもない。
source_examples.translation_en: It's impossible to solve this problem.

source_examples.japanese: これ以上我慢しようもない。
source_examples.translation_en: It's impossible to endure any further.

source_examples.japanese: 彼には通じようもない。
source_examples.translation_en: There's no way to get through to him.

source_examples.japanese: その薬は飲みようもない。
source_examples.translation_en: It's impossible to take (swallow) that medicine.

source_title: Verbる がままに (〜ga mama ni)
source_short_explanation: Expresses 'letting something happen as it is'; 'just as something does'.
source_long_explanation: がままに describes an action happening exactly 'as is,' without intervention or change, often suggesting doing something passively or naturally.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + がままに

source_examples.japanese: 窓を開けるがままにしておいたら、風が部屋に入ってきました。
source_examples.translation_en: I left the window open as it was, and the wind came into the room.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は涙を流すがままに、ただ黙って座っていた。
source_examples.translation_en: She just sat quietly, letting her tears flow.

source_examples.japanese: 子供たちは笑うがままに、公園で走り回っていた。
source_examples.translation_en: The children ran around the park, laughing freely as they pleased.

source_examples.japanese: 日が沈むがままに、私たちは海辺で話し続けました。
source_examples.translation_en: We kept talking by the sea, letting the sun set as it would.

source_title: Verbる が早いか (verb-ru ga hayai ka)
source_short_explanation: Expresses 'as soon as...' or 'the moment when...'.
source_long_explanation: Verbる が早いか indicates that something happens immediately after something else. It's similar to 'as soon as...' or 'no sooner than...'.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + が早いか

source_examples.japanese: 部屋に入るが早いか、彼はテレビをつけた。
source_examples.translation_en: No sooner had he entered the room than he turned on the TV.

source_examples.japanese: 電車に乗るが早いか、私はすぐに眠ってしまった。
source_examples.translation_en: As soon as I got on the train, I immediately fell asleep.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女が見るが早いか、すぐに泣き始めた。
source_examples.translation_en: The moment she looked, she began to cry.

source_examples.japanese: 給料をもらうが早いか、全て使い果たしてしまった。
source_examples.translation_en: No sooner had I received my salary than I spent it all.

source_title: Verbる くらいなら (〜ru kurai nara)
source_short_explanation: Expresses preference to avoid something: 'rather than...', 'if it comes to doing X, I'd rather...'.
source_long_explanation: This grammar is used when the speaker would rather not do something or chooses another option rather than face the stated action. It’s often translated as 'rather than... I'd prefer...' or 'if it comes down to doing X, I'd rather...'.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + くらいなら

source_examples.japanese: 一人で行くくらいなら、家にいるほうがましです。
source_examples.translation_en: I'd rather stay at home than go alone.

source_examples.japanese: 負けるくらいなら、試合をしないほうがいい。
source_examples.translation_en: Rather than lose, it's better not to compete.

source_examples.japanese: 遅刻するくらいなら、一日休んだほうがいい。
source_examples.translation_en: It's better to take a day off than to be late.

source_examples.japanese: 痛い目に遭うくらいなら、そのリスクは避けます。
source_examples.translation_en: I'd rather avoid that risk than suffer the consequences.

source_title: Verbる こと なし に (Verb-ru koto nashi ni)
source_short_explanation: Used to express 'without doing something'.
source_long_explanation: Verbることなしに indicates doing something else 'without' performing the stated action. It can imply skipping or omitting the verb action entirely.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + ことなしに

source_examples.japanese: 試験を勉強することなしに、合格しました。
source_examples.translation_en: I passed the exam without studying.

source_examples.japanese: 試着することなしに、服を買いました。
source_examples.translation_en: I bought the clothes without trying them on.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は働くことなしに生活しています。
source_examples.translation_en: He is living without working.

source_examples.japanese: 手続きをすることなしに、退職しました。
source_examples.translation_en: I retired without going through any procedures.

source_title: Verbる ことのないように (Verb-ru koto no nai you ni)
source_short_explanation: Expresses the desire or effort to prevent something: 'so as not to...', 'to avoid...'.
source_long_explanation: Verbる ことのないように is used to show that one is trying or intending to prevent some action from happening. It's like 'so that this doesn't happen' or 'in order not to...'.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + ことのないように

source_examples.japanese: 車をなくすことのないように、駐車場で必ずロックしましょう。
source_examples.translation_en: Lock your car in the parking lot so you don't lose it.

source_examples.japanese: 風邪を引くことのないように、手をよく洗いましょう。
source_examples.translation_en: Wash your hands well so you don't catch a cold.

source_examples.japanese: 試験に落ちることのないように、毎日勉強しましょう。
source_examples.translation_en: Study every day so you don't fail the exam.

source_examples.japanese: 間違いをすることのないように、仕事を慎重に行いましょう。
source_examples.translation_en: Let's work carefully to avoid making mistakes.

source_title: Verbる ときりがない (verb-ru to kiri ga nai)
source_short_explanation: Used to indicate that something can go on endlessly or without limits.
source_long_explanation: The ～るときりがない grammar point is used to express that once you start doing the verb, there’s no end or limit. The phrase 'きりがない' means 'no end' or 'endless.'
source_formation: Verb-casual + と + きりがない

source_examples.japanese: 彼の悪口を言うときりがない。
source_examples.translation_en: If we start talking about his faults, there's no end.

source_examples.japanese: その問題を考えるときりがない。
source_examples.translation_en: If you start thinking about that problem, there's no end.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女の美点を挙げるときりがない。
source_examples.translation_en: If you start listing her virtues, there would be no end.

source_examples.japanese: この世でおいしいものを食べるときりがない。
source_examples.translation_en: If you start eating all the delicious things in this world, there's no end.

source_title: Verbる ともなく Verb (Verb-ru tomonaku Verb)
source_short_explanation: Used to express 'without a particular intention', 'unconsciously', or 'before one knows it'.
source_long_explanation: The phrase VerbるともなくVerb indicates doing something unintentionally or unconsciously— you just find yourself doing it without a clear aim or intention.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + ともなく + Verb

source_examples.japanese: 遠くを見るともなく窓の外を眺めた。
source_examples.translation_en: I found myself gazing out the window, not really looking at anything in particular.

source_examples.japanese: 知るともなく、彼が去ったことを感じた。
source_examples.translation_en: Without really knowing, I felt that he had left.

source_examples.japanese: 本を読むともなく、ページをめくっていた。
source_examples.translation_en: Without intending to read, I was just flipping through the pages of the book.

source_examples.japanese: 寝るともなく、ベッドに横になっていた。
source_examples.translation_en: I was lying in bed without really intending to sleep.

source_title: Verbる ともなしに Verb (Verb-ru tomonashi ni Verb)
source_short_explanation: Expresses doing something unintentionally or without conscious thought.
source_long_explanation: VerbるともなしにVerb is used to show that you do some action without particularly intending to. Often you ‘end up doing’ something by habit or casually.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + ともなしに + Verb

source_examples.japanese: 本を読むともなしに眠ってしまった。
source_examples.translation_en: I ended up falling asleep while reading the book without really meaning to.

source_examples.japanese: 軽い気持ちで手紙を書くともなしに、彼に本心を告白した。
source_examples.translation_en: While writing a letter casually, I ended up confessing my true feelings to him.

source_examples.japanese: 散歩をするともなしに、新しいカフェを見つけた。
source_examples.translation_en: While I was walking with no particular destination, I found a new cafe.

source_examples.japanese: 洋服を整理するともなしに、昔の写真を見つけた。
source_examples.translation_en: As I was absentmindedly organizing clothes, I came across some old photos.

source_short_explanation: Expresses 'as soon as' or 'the moment'.
source_long_explanation: Verbるなり indicates that the following action happens immediately after the verb action. It can be translated as 'no sooner than...', 'as soon as...', or 'the moment...'.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + なり

source_examples.japanese: 家に帰るなり、すぐに寝た。
source_examples.translation_en: As soon as I got home, I went to sleep.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が駅に着くなり、電話をかけてきた。
source_examples.translation_en: He called me the moment he arrived at the station.

source_examples.japanese: ドアを開けるなり、犬が吠え始めた。
source_examples.translation_en: As soon as I opened the door, the dog started barking.

source_examples.japanese: テストが終わるなり、彼は教室を出て行った。
source_examples.translation_en: He left the classroom the moment the test ended.

source_title: Verbる にとどまらず～も (Verb-ru ni todomarazu ~ mo)
source_short_explanation: Expresses 'not only… but also', 'not limited to…'.
source_long_explanation: にとどまらず is used to indicate that something goes beyond just the stated verb or noun. It can be translated as 'not just… but also…' or 'not limited to…'.
source_formation: Noun / Verb-dictionary form + にとどまらず + も/ほかのこと

source_examples.japanese: 彼は仕事にとどまらず、ボランティア活動もしている。
source_examples.translation_en: He does not just work; he also does volunteer activities.

source_examples.japanese: この機能は写真撮影にとどまらず、動画撮影も可能です。
source_examples.translation_en: This function is not limited to taking photos; it can also record videos.

source_examples.japanese: このレストランは日本料理にとどまらず、中華料理も提供しています。
source_examples.translation_en: This restaurant not only serves Japanese food, but also Chinese cuisine.

source_examples.japanese: その企業は製造業にとどまらず、流通業務も手がけている。
source_examples.translation_en: That company’s operations go beyond manufacturing; they also handle distribution.

source_title: Verbる にはあたらない (Verb-ru ni wa ataranai)
source_short_explanation: Used to say 'there is no need to...', 'it’s not necessary to...'.
source_long_explanation: Verbる にはあたらない expresses that something is not worth the reaction or there is no need to do the verb. It's somewhat formal and often used in writing.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + にはあたらない

source_examples.japanese: パニックに陥るにはあたらない。
source_examples.translation_en: There’s no need to panic.

source_examples.japanese: 彼に謝るにはあたらない。
source_examples.translation_en: There’s no need to apologize to him.

source_examples.japanese: そのようなことを心配するにはあたらない。
source_examples.translation_en: It’s not worth worrying about such things.

source_examples.japanese: それについて深く考えるにはあたらない。
source_examples.translation_en: There’s no need to think too deeply about it.

source_short_explanation: Indicates that doing the verb is impossible or difficult, even if one wants to.
source_long_explanation: Verbる にも is often used with an additional clause explaining why the action can’t be done. It can be translated as 'even if (I) want to do X, I can’t (because...)'.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + にも + (reason it can't be done)

source_examples.japanese: 明日雨が降ったとしても、傘を持つにも荷物が多すぎる。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if it rains tomorrow, I have too much luggage to bring an umbrella.

source_examples.japanese: 試験に落ちたが、もう一度受けるにもお金が足りない。
source_examples.translation_en: I failed the exam, but I don’t have the money to take it again even if I wanted to.

source_examples.japanese: 彼に会いたいと思っても、彼に会うにも難しい状況だ。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if I want to see him, it's a difficult situation to meet him.

source_examples.japanese: この空港から彼女の家に行くにもタクシーが必要だ。
source_examples.translation_en: I'd need a taxi to get from this airport to her house, even if I wanted to go.

source_title: Verbる にも Verb れない (Verb-ru ni mo Verb-re nai)
source_short_explanation: Expresses: 'Even if I try/want to do something, I cannot.'
source_long_explanation: This pattern emphasizes that a person wants or attempts to do something (often in volitional form), but is incapable of doing so. It is often used with potential verbs in negative form: 'Even if I try to ~, I can't ~.'
source_formation: Verb-volitional + にも + Verb-potential negative

source_examples.japanese: 彼を理解しようにも理解できない。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if I try to understand him, I can't.

source_examples.japanese: 走ろうにも走れない。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if I want to run, I can't.

source_examples.japanese: 泣こうにも泣けない。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if I want to cry, I can't.

source_examples.japanese: 忘れようにも忘れられない。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if I try to forget, I just can’t.

source_title: Verbる べからざる Noun (Verb-ru bekara zaru Noun)
source_short_explanation: Used to express what should not be done; 'must not', 'should not'.
source_long_explanation: The Japanese grammar point Verbる べからざる Noun is used to indicate something that should not be done, or is not allowed to be done. It translates to 'must not' or 'should not' in English. It is often used in formal written Japanese or in formal speeches. It is constructed by using the verb in its dictionary form followed by 'べからざる' and a noun, usually related to behavior or events.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + べからざる + Noun

source_examples.japanese: 人を裏切るべからざる行為だ。
source_examples.translation_en: Betraying others is an act that must not be done.

source_examples.japanese: 子供を傷つけるべからざる行動だ。
source_examples.translation_en: Hurting a child is a behavior that must not happen.

source_examples.japanese: 公に嘘をつくべからざる行動だ。
source_examples.translation_en: Lying publicly is an act that should not be done.

source_examples.japanese: 他人の財産を侵すべからざる行為だ。
source_examples.translation_en: Infringing on someone else’s property is an act that must not be performed.

source_title: Verbる べからず (〜ru bekara zu)
source_short_explanation: Expresses the idea of 'must not do' or 'should not do'.
source_long_explanation: The ～るべからず grammar point is used to express a strong prohibition or firmly established rule. It can be translated as 'must not do' or 'should not do'. It is common in formal or instructive settings (e.g., signs, notices). The formation is straightforward with verbs in dictionary form followed by べからず.
source_formation: Verb-ru + べからず

source_examples.japanese: 嘘をつくべからず。
source_examples.translation_en: One must not tell lies.

source_examples.japanese: 彼らの秘密を漏らすべからず。
source_examples.translation_en: You must not leak their secrets.

source_examples.japanese: ルールを破るべからず。
source_examples.translation_en: You must not break the rules.

source_examples.japanese: 勉強を怠るべからず。
source_examples.translation_en: One must not neglect their studies.

source_short_explanation: Expresses the meaning of 'in order to', 'for the purpose of'.
source_long_explanation: The 'Verbる べく' grammar point is used to indicate a strong intention or purpose of the speaker. It can be translated as 'in order to' or 'for the purpose of' in English. It is more common in written language or formal contexts.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + べく

source_examples.japanese: 成功するべく、日々努力しています。
source_examples.translation_en: In order to succeed, I am working hard every day.

source_examples.japanese: 健康を維持するべく、毎日運動をしています。
source_examples.translation_en: In order to maintain my health, I exercise every day.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は学位を得るべく、毎日勉強しています。
source_examples.translation_en: He studies every day in order to get a degree.

source_examples.japanese: 早く目的地に到着するべく、タクシーを呼びました。
source_examples.translation_en: I called a taxi in order to arrive at the destination quickly.

source_title: Verbる べくもない (Verb-ru beku mo nai)
source_short_explanation: Means 'it's impossible to...' or 'there's no way to...'.
source_long_explanation: This grammar point is used when you want to express that something is impossible or there is no way to do something. The verb before 'べくもない' should be in its dictionary form.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + べくもない

source_examples.japanese: その問題はとても難しく、解くべくもない。
source_examples.translation_en: That problem is so difficult that it's impossible to solve.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女はあまりに速く走って、追いつくべくもない。
source_examples.translation_en: She runs so fast that there's no way to catch up.

source_examples.japanese: 試験の筆記用具を忘れた。書くべくもない。
source_examples.translation_en: I forgot my writing utensils for the test. It's impossible to write.

source_examples.japanese: 彼はとても高く跳ぶ。追い越すべくもない。
source_examples.translation_en: He jumps so high that there's no way to surpass him.

source_title: Verbる までもない (〜ru made mo nai)
source_short_explanation: It's not necessary to the extent of; no need to.
source_long_explanation: The 〜るまでもない grammar point is used to express that something is not necessary to the extent of doing that action. It can be translated as 'no need to' in English.
source_formation: Verb-る + までもない

source_examples.japanese: そんなに心配するまでもない。
source_examples.translation_en: There's no need to worry that much.

source_examples.japanese: 電話するまでもないことだ。
source_examples.translation_en: It's not something you need to call about.

source_examples.japanese: 小さな失敗であきらめるまでもない。
source_examples.translation_en: You don't need to give up over a small mistake.

source_examples.japanese: この問題は、会議で話し合うまでもない。
source_examples.translation_en: This problem doesn't need to be discussed at a meeting.

source_title: Verbる ものとする (〜ru mono to suru)
source_short_explanation: Assuming or deciding something as...
source_long_explanation: The ～るものとする grammar point is often used in formal or legal contexts to express a decision or assumption. It can be translated as 'it is decided/assumed that...' or 'shall be deemed that...'.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + ものとする

source_examples.japanese: ここでの話し合いは秘密とするものとします。
source_examples.translation_en: The discussions here are to be kept confidential.

source_examples.japanese: この契約は明日から有効とするものとする。
source_examples.translation_en: This contract shall become effective from tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: 彼をチームのリーダーとするものとします。
source_examples.translation_en: We will designate him as the team leader.

source_examples.japanese: この件については終了とするものとする。
source_examples.translation_en: We will consider this matter closed.

source_title: Verbる や否や (Verb-ru ya ina ya)
source_short_explanation: Expresses the idea of 'as soon as', 'the moment...'.
source_long_explanation: The grammar point Verbる や否や is used to express something happening immediately after another action or event. It can be translated as 'as soon as...' or 'the moment...'. The verb must be in dictionary form.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + や否や

source_examples.japanese: 彼女が家に帰るや否や、すぐにテレビをつけました。
source_examples.translation_en: As soon as she returned home, she turned on the TV.

source_examples.japanese: 私が郵便箱を開けるや否や、手紙が落ちました。
source_examples.translation_en: The moment I opened the mailbox, the letters fell out.

source_examples.japanese: 子供たちは学校が終わるや否や、公園に走りました。
source_examples.translation_en: As soon as school was over, the children ran to the park.

source_examples.japanese: 父が新聞を読むや否や、何かに震えていました。
source_examples.translation_en: The moment my father read the newspaper, he started trembling about something.

source_title: Verbる 始末だ (〜ru shimatsu da)
source_short_explanation: Indicates a (often unfortunate) result or conclusion of an action.
source_long_explanation: The ～る始末だ grammar point expresses the outcome or conclusion of an action, typically a negative or unfortunate result. It can be translated as 'end up...', 'the result is...', or 'the conclusion is...'.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + 始末だ

source_examples.japanese: 忘れてしまって、パスポートを家に置いてくる始末だった。
source_examples.translation_en: I ended up leaving my passport at home because I forgot.

source_examples.japanese: 毎晩遅くまで働いて、倒れる始末だ。
source_examples.translation_en: I work until late every night and end up collapsing.

source_examples.japanese: 勉強しなかったので、試験に落ちる始末だ。
source_examples.translation_en: I didn't study, so I ended up failing the exam.

source_examples.japanese: 電車が遅れたため、会議に遅れる始末だ。
source_examples.translation_en: Because the train was delayed, I ended up being late for the meeting.

source_title: Verbる 嫌いがある (～ru kirai ga aru)
source_short_explanation: Tendency to do a negative action; have a bad habit of ~.
source_long_explanation: The ～る嫌いがある grammar point is used to express a negative tendency or habit. It often carries a critical or disapproving tone and points out someone's habitual action.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + 嫌いがある

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は遅刻する嫌いがある。
source_examples.translation_en: She has a tendency to be late.

source_examples.japanese: 私の父はお酒を飲み過ぎる嫌いがある。
source_examples.translation_en: My father has a habit of drinking too much alcohol.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は物をすぐ忘れる嫌いがある。
source_examples.translation_en: He tends to forget things quickly.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は人の話を途中で切る嫌いがある。
source_examples.translation_en: She has a habit of interrupting people while they are speaking.

source_title: いつまで～のやら (itsumade ~ no yara)
source_short_explanation: Expresses uncertainty regarding duration; 'don't know when... will end'.
source_long_explanation: The いつまで～のやら grammar point is used to express uncertainty about when something will end or finish. It is often used in situations where the speaker is unsure about when a particular state of affairs or event will conclude.
source_formation: いつまで + Verb (dictionary form) + のやら

source_examples.japanese: この試験勉強はいつまで続くのやら。
source_examples.translation_en: I don't know when this exam study will end.

source_examples.japanese: 彼の話がいつ終わるのやら、わからない。
source_examples.translation_en: I don't know when his talk will finish.

source_examples.japanese: この雨がいつまで降り続くのやら。
source_examples.translation_en: I don't know when this rain will stop.

source_examples.japanese: コロナのパンデミックがいつまで続くのやら。
source_examples.translation_en: I don't know when this coronavirus pandemic will end.

source_title: ～が Verb られる (〜ga Verb rareru)
source_short_explanation: Expresses potential or ability to do something; 'can', 'able to'.
source_long_explanation: The ～が Verb られる grammar pattern generally refers to the potential form of Japanese verbs (i.e., 'can do something'). However, the exact formation depends on the verb group. For most Group 1 (五段) verbs, potential form changes the final -u to -eru (e.g., 書く→書ける). For Group 2 (一段) verbs, you often see ～られる (e.g., 食べる→食べられる). In English, it translates as 'can' or 'able to'.
source_formation:
❶ (Group 1) Verb:  書く → 書ける / 飲む → 飲める, etc.
❷ (Group 2) Verb-ます stem + られる (食べる→食べられる、見る→見られる)

source_examples.japanese: 彼がこの問題を解けると思いますか？
source_examples.translation_en: Do you think he can solve this problem?

source_examples.japanese: 私がその大きな箱を運べるか？
source_examples.translation_en: Can I carry that big box?

source_examples.japanese: 彼が早く走れると思います。
source_examples.translation_en: I think he can run fast.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は日本語が話せる。
source_examples.translation_en: She can speak Japanese.

source_short_explanation: Expressing unexpected outcomes; 'just when I thought...', 'but...'.
source_long_explanation: The ～かと思いきや grammar point is used when the outcome turns out different from what was initially assumed or expected. It can be translated as 'just when I thought...' or simply 'but (actually)...'. It often highlights that the speaker’s assumption was proven wrong by subsequent events.
source_formation: Sentence + かと思いきや (Verb plain form, i-/na-Adjective, or Noun + だ + かと思いきや)

source_examples.japanese: 明日は晴れるかと思いきや、まさかの雨が降った。
source_examples.translation_en: I thought it would be sunny tomorrow, but unexpectedly it rained.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が試験に落ちたかと思いきや、合格していた。
source_examples.translation_en: I thought he had failed the test, but he actually passed.

source_examples.japanese: このケーキは美味しそうだったかと思いきや、全然甘くなかった。
source_examples.translation_en: I thought this cake would be delicious, but it wasn’t sweet at all.

source_examples.japanese: 列車が遅れるかと思いきや、時間通りに到着した。
source_examples.translation_en: I thought the train would be late, but it arrived on time.

source_short_explanation: Expresses the reason or cause; 'because', 'due to', 'as a result of'.
source_long_explanation: The ～がゆえに grammar point is used to express a reason or cause, often in more formal writing or speech. It roughly corresponds to 'because (of)', 'due to', or 'as a result of' in English.
source_formation: Noun / Verb / Adjective + がゆえに

source_examples.japanese: 愛情がゆえに、彼は彼女を許した。
source_examples.translation_en: Because of love, he forgave her.

source_examples.japanese: 突然の雨がゆえに、試合は延期された。
source_examples.translation_en: Due to the sudden rain, the match was postponed.

source_examples.japanese: 彼の努力がゆえに、彼は成功を収めた。
source_examples.translation_en: Because of his efforts, he achieved success.

source_examples.japanese: 彼の死がゆえに、彼の家族は深い悲しみに包まれた。
source_examples.translation_en: Due to his death, his family was enveloped in deep sorrow.

source_title: ～がゆえの Noun (〜ga yue no Noun)
source_short_explanation: Expresses the reason or cause for something; 'because of', 'due to'.
source_long_explanation: The ～がゆえの Noun pattern is used to describe a noun that exists or occurs due to some cause. It is often used in more literary or formal contexts.
source_formation: Noun / Verb-dictionary form + がゆえの + Noun

source_examples.japanese: 愛がゆえの悲しみ。
source_examples.translation_en: Sadness due to love.

source_examples.japanese: 健康がゆえの幸せ。
source_examples.translation_en: Happiness due to good health.

source_examples.japanese: 悪行がゆえの罰。
source_examples.translation_en: Punishment due to wrongdoing.

source_examples.japanese: 努力がゆえの成功。
source_examples.translation_en: Success due to effort.

source_title: ～から Noun に 至る まで (〜kara 〜ni itaru made)
source_short_explanation: Expressing range from one thing to another; 'from...to', 'ranging from...to'.
source_long_explanation: The ～から〜に至るまで grammar point emphasizes a range or scope extending from one extreme to another. It can be translated as 'from...to...' or 'ranging from...to...' in English. It can apply to people, places, times, objects, and so on.
source_formation: Noun (start) + から + Noun (end) + に至るまで

source_examples.japanese: このバンドの曲は、青年から老人に至るまで、人々に愛されています。
source_examples.translation_en: The songs of this band are loved by people ranging from the young to the elderly.

source_examples.japanese: 小さい物件から大きな建物に至るまで、全てのプロパティの管理を我々が行います。
source_examples.translation_en: We handle all property management, ranging from small units to large buildings.

source_examples.japanese: 朝のニュース放送から夜のドラマに至るまで、テレビは毎日見ています。
source_examples.translation_en: I watch TV every day, from the morning news broadcasts to the night dramas.

source_examples.japanese: この地域は、春から冬に至るまで旅行者で賑わいます。
source_examples.translation_en: This area is bustling with tourists from spring to winter.

source_short_explanation: To seem like; as if; as though.
source_long_explanation: The ～ごとく grammar point is used to express similarity or resemblance. It is quite formal/literary, meaning 'as if,' 'as though,' or 'like.' It can be used with verbs and nouns.
source_formation: Verb-て + ごとく / Noun + の + ごとく

source_examples.japanese: 彼は鳥のごとく飛んでいるように見えた。
source_examples.translation_en: He looked as though he was flying like a bird.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は死んだごとく眠っていた。
source_examples.translation_en: He was sleeping as though he were dead.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女はアイドルのごとく崇められている。
source_examples.translation_en: She is revered as if she were an idol.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は風のごとく走った。
source_examples.translation_en: He ran like the wind.

source_short_explanation: Used to express the reason or premise for a decision or judgment; 'since', 'because'.
source_long_explanation: The ～こととて grammar point expresses a reason or premise in a slightly formal or literary way. It can often be interpreted as 'since' or 'because'.
source_formation: Verb (plain form) + こととて / Noun + の + こととて / (な-Adjective + な) + こととて

source_examples.japanese: 彼は裁判に勝つために全資産を使うこととて、弁護士に頼んだ。
source_examples.translation_en: Since he's using all his assets to win the trial, he hired a lawyer.

source_examples.japanese: 明日は大切な試験があることとて、今夜は早く寝ます。
source_examples.translation_en: Since I have an important exam tomorrow, I’m going to bed early tonight.

source_examples.japanese: このプロジェクトの成功は会社の未来に影響することとて、全力を尽くします。
source_examples.translation_en: Because the success of this project will affect the company's future, I will do my best.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が有名人であることとて、プライバシーが保護されるべきだ。
source_examples.translation_en: Since he is a celebrity, his privacy should be protected.

source_short_explanation: Expresses the idea of 'was able to do without'; 'managed to avoid'.
source_long_explanation: The ～ずにすんだ grammar point indicates that one was able to avoid doing something or managed to get by without doing it. It translates as 'managed to avoid ~' or 'got by without ~.'
source_formation: Verb-ず form + に + すんだ

source_examples.japanese: 彼は事故を起こさずにすんだ。
source_examples.translation_en: He managed to avoid having an accident.

source_examples.japanese: 私は手術せずにすんだ。
source_examples.translation_en: I was able to do without surgery.

source_examples.japanese: 雨が降らずにすんだ。
source_examples.translation_en: We managed to avoid the rain.

source_examples.japanese: 罰金を払わずにすんだ。
source_examples.translation_en: I managed to avoid paying a fine.

source_title: ～だろうとなかろうと (〜darou to nakarou to)
source_short_explanation: Expresses 'regardless of whether it is or isn't'.
source_long_explanation: The ～だろうとなかろうと grammar point is used to express the idea of 'regardless of whether it is or isn't.' It translates roughly as 'whether it is ~ or not' in English. This construction emphasizes that the speaker’s stance or action does not change, regardless of the two possible conditions.
source_formation: Noun / i-Adjective / na-Adjective / Verb + だろうとなかろうと

source_examples.japanese: 試験が難しいだろうとなかろうと、全力で頑張ります。
source_examples.translation_en: Regardless of whether the exam is difficult or not, I will do my best.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が来るだろうとなかろうと、私たちは始めます。
source_examples.translation_en: Whether he comes or not, we will start.

source_examples.japanese: この仕事が面白いだろうとなかろうと、私は続けます。
source_examples.translation_en: Whether this job is interesting or not, I will continue.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が賛成するだろうとなかろうと、私たちは進行します。
source_examples.translation_en: Whether he agrees or not, we will proceed.

source_short_explanation: Expresses the speaker's intention or plan.
source_long_explanation: The ～つもりだ grammar point is used to express the speaker's intention or plan to do something. It translates as 'intend to,' 'plan to,' or 'think that (I will).' It's often used with the verb in its dictionary form.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + つもりだ

source_examples.japanese: 明日は早く起きるつもりです。
source_examples.translation_en: I plan to wake up early tomorrow.

source_examples.japanese: 私は日本語を勉強するつもりです。
source_examples.translation_en: I intend to study Japanese.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は留学するつもりだと言った。
source_examples.translation_en: He said he plans to study abroad.

source_examples.japanese: 私は来週末に家族と旅行するつもりだ。
source_examples.translation_en: I plan to travel with my family next weekend.

source_short_explanation: Expresses the speaker's intention or plan; 'with the intention of', 'planning to'.
source_long_explanation: The ～つもりで grammar point is used to express the speaker's intention or mindset when doing something. It can often be translated as 'with the intention of' or 'with the mindset that.'
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + つもりで

source_examples.japanese: 私は日本に住むつもりで日本語を勉強しています。
source_examples.translation_en: I am studying Japanese with the intention of living in Japan.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は全てを失うつもりでギャンブルをしました。
source_examples.translation_en: He gambled with the intention of risking everything.

source_examples.japanese: 明日のテストに合格するつもりで一生懸命勉強します。
source_examples.translation_en: I will study hard with the intention of passing tomorrow’s test.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は早く起きるつもりで早く寝ました。
source_examples.translation_en: He went to bed early with the intention of waking up early.

source_short_explanation: Expresses that just doing something is not enough or will not suffice.
source_long_explanation: The grammar point ～ではすまない is used when the speaker strongly feels that an action or situation alone is not sufficient or acceptable, implying that more serious measures are needed or that the consequences are more severe.
source_formation: Verb-dictionary form + ではすまない / い-Adjective + ではすまない / な-Adjective + ではすまない / Noun + ではすまない

source_examples.japanese: ただ謝るではすまない。何か行動を取らなければならない。
source_examples.translation_en: Just apologizing will not suffice. Some action needs to be taken.

source_examples.japanese: この問題は議論だけではすまない。具体的な計画が必要だ。
source_examples.translation_en: This problem won't be solved with just discussions. A concrete plan is needed.

source_examples.japanese: 彼の失敗は注意だけではすまない。彼はその責任を取るべきだ。
source_examples.translation_en: His failure won't be resolved with just a warning. He should take responsibility.

source_examples.japanese: この失敗は金だけではすまない。信頼を取り戻すため、真心で謝罪するべきだ。
source_examples.translation_en: This mistake cannot be settled with money alone. To regain trust, an earnest apology is needed.

source_short_explanation: Expresses a special situation or event due to certain circumstances.
source_long_explanation: The ～とあって grammar point is used to indicate that, due to a special or noteworthy circumstance, a particular situation has occurred. It often translates as 'because (it is)...' or 'given that...' in English, emphasizing the uniqueness of the cause.
source_formation: Noun + とあって / (Sometimes Verb + とあって, depending on context)

source_examples.japanese: 春休みとあって、公園は子供たちでいっぱいだ。
source_examples.translation_en: Because it's spring break, the park is full of children.

source_examples.japanese: 試験前とあって、図書館は学生で混んでいる。
source_examples.translation_en: With exams coming up, the library is crowded with students.

source_examples.japanese: 開店日とあって、その店にはたくさんの人が並んでいた。
source_examples.translation_en: Because it was the store's opening day, a lot of people lined up.

source_examples.japanese: 彼の誕生日とあって、友人たちはサプライズパーティーを計画した。
source_examples.translation_en: Because it was his birthday, his friends planned a surprise party.

source_short_explanation: Expresses a condition; 'if', 'when', 'since'.
source_long_explanation: The ～とあれば grammar point is used to express a condition or premise in which a certain outcome or action naturally follows. It can be translated as 'if,' 'when,' or 'since,' depending on context. It emphasizes that under this specific condition, a certain response is expected.
source_formation: Verb-casual + とあれば / い-Adjective + とあれば / な-Adjective + だとあれば / Noun + だとあれば

source_examples.japanese: 無料とあれば、誰でも利用したいと思います。
source_examples.translation_en: If it's free, anyone would want to use it.

source_examples.japanese: この曲が流れるとあれば、彼は必ず踊り始めます。
source_examples.translation_en: If this song starts playing, he will definitely begin to dance.

source_examples.japanese: 明日が休日だとあれば、今夜は遅くまで起きていられます。
source_examples.translation_en: If tomorrow is a holiday, I can stay up late tonight.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が参加するとあれば、このイベントは成功でしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: If he participates, this event will surely be successful.

source_short_explanation: Even if it is said that; Even though; Although.
source_long_explanation: The ～といえども grammar point is used to show a contrast or contradiction. It is similar to 'even though' or 'although' in English. It can be used with nouns, verbs, adjectives, etc., to emphasize that the reality is different from the assumption or label.
source_formation: Noun + といえども / Verb-plain form + といえども / Adjective + といえども

source_examples.japanese: 彼が天才といえども、ミスをすることはあります。
source_examples.translation_en: Even though he’s a genius, he still makes mistakes.

source_examples.japanese: このパソコンが新しいといえども、問題があります。
source_examples.translation_en: Even though this computer is new, it has problems.

source_examples.japanese: 春といえども、まだ寒い日があります。
source_examples.translation_en: Even though it's spring, there are still cold days.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女が一番好きな人といえども、嫌なことは嫌です。
source_examples.translation_en: Even though she’s my favorite person, unpleasant things are still unpleasant.

pattern: といったらありはしない
source_title: ～といったらありはしない (〜to ittara ari wa shinai)
source_short_explanation: Express extreme exclamation; 'extremely', 'unbelievable', 'unsurpassed'.
source_long_explanation: The ～といったらありはしない grammar point is used to express an extreme degree of something, often surprise or admiration. It can be loosely translated as 'unbelievably...' or 'incredibly...'.
source_formation: Noun + といったらありはしない / な-Adjective + といったらありはしない

source_examples.japanese: 彼の英語の上手さといったらありはしない。
source_examples.translation_en: His English is unbelievably good.

source_examples.japanese: このスイーツの美味しさといったらありはしない。
source_examples.translation_en: These sweets are unbelievably delicious.

source_examples.japanese: その子の頭の良さといったらありはしない。
source_examples.translation_en: That kid's intelligence is unsurpassed.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女の美しさといったらありはしない。
source_examples.translation_en: Her beauty is beyond belief.

pattern: といったらありゃしない
source_title: ～といったらありゃしない (〜to ittara arya shinai)
source_short_explanation: Emphasizes that something is to the extreme; 'you have no idea how...', 'it's incredibly...'.
source_long_explanation: The ～といったらありゃしない grammar point is an idiomatic expression used to emphasize that something is extremely or incredibly a certain way—often beyond words. It can be loosely rendered as 'you wouldn't believe how...' or 'it's indescribably...'.
source_formation: Verb-casual + といったらありゃしない / い-Adjective + といったらありゃしない / な-Adjective + だ + といったらありゃしない / Noun + だ + といったらありゃしない

source_examples.japanese: その店のラーメンは美味しいといったらありゃしない。
source_examples.translation_en: You have no idea how delicious the ramen at that shop is.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女の料理の腕前は上手だといったらありゃしない。
source_examples.translation_en: You have no idea how skilled she is at cooking.

source_examples.japanese: この冬の寒さは厳しいといったらありゃしない。
source_examples.translation_en: You have no idea how harsh this winter's cold is.

source_examples.japanese: その小説は面白いといったらありゃしない。
source_examples.translation_en: You have no idea how interesting that novel is.

source_short_explanation: Expresses the extreme of something; 'nothing can be more ... than this'.
source_long_explanation: The ～といったらない grammar point is used to emphasize the high degree or intensity of an action or state. It can be translated as “nothing can be more ... than this” or “it’s extremely...”. It conveys that something is so intense or extreme that it cannot be adequately described.
source_formation: い-Adjective + といったらない / な-Adjective + だといったらない / Noun + だといったらない

source_examples.japanese: 今日は寒いといったらない。
source_examples.translation_en: It’s extremely cold today.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女の料理の美味しさといったらない。
source_examples.translation_en: Nothing can be more delicious than her cooking.

source_examples.japanese: この子の頭の良さだといったらない。
source_examples.translation_en: This child is unbelievably smart.

source_examples.japanese: 彼の怠けっぷりだといったらない。
source_examples.translation_en: Nobody could be lazier than him.

source_short_explanation: Highlights a situation or condition that is serious/extreme, often with a negative nuance.
source_long_explanation: The grammar point ～ときている is used to emphasize that some circumstance is particularly notable—often negatively. It implies, “Given that things are so ~, it’s no wonder that...” or “Because the situation is (too) ~, such-and-such follows.” It is relatively informal and more common in spoken language.
source_formation: Verb-casual / い-Adjective / な-Adjective（＋だ） / Noun（＋だ） + ときている

source_examples.japanese: 仕事が忙しいときているので、なかなか休みが取れません。
source_examples.translation_en: Because work is so busy, I just can’t take any time off.

source_examples.japanese: 経済が悪いときているだけに、会社が大量解雇を発表した。
source_examples.translation_en: Since the economy is in such bad shape, the company announced mass layoffs.

source_examples.japanese: 旅行先で荷物を盗まれたときているから、旅行を楽しむどころではない。
source_examples.translation_en: Given that my luggage was stolen while traveling, there’s no way I can enjoy the trip.

source_examples.japanese: 試験が近いときているうえに、課題も山ほどあって大変だ。
source_examples.translation_en: Not only are exams coming up, but I also have a mountain of assignments, so it’s really tough.

source_short_explanation: Indicates a contrasting or inconvenient timing; 'just when...', 'even though...'.
source_long_explanation: The grammar point ～ところを is often used when something happens (or one acts) at a certain moment/condition that makes the timing inconvenient or contrary to what is expected. It can imply “in spite of the fact that...” or “just when...” depending on context.
source_formation: Verb-ている + ところを / Noun + の + ところを / い-Adjective + ところを / な-Adjective + な + ところを

source_examples.japanese: ちょうど映画を見ているところを、停電で真っ暗になった。
source_examples.translation_en: Just when I was in the middle of watching a movie, the power went out and everything went dark.

source_examples.japanese: 美味しく食べているところを、彼が全部横取りしてしまった。
source_examples.translation_en: Right when I was enjoying my meal, he took it all away.

source_examples.japanese: 飛行機が離陸しようとしているところを、急にエンジンが止まった。
source_examples.translation_en: Just as the plane was about to take off, the engine suddenly stopped.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女が怒っているところを、私は冗談を言ってしまった。
source_examples.translation_en: Even though she was angry, I went ahead and made a joke.

source_short_explanation: Indicates a general belief or widely accepted view; 'is considered', 'is seen as', 'is said to be'.
source_long_explanation: The ～とされる grammar point expresses what is generally believed, accepted, or reputed. It can be translated as 'is considered to be,' 'is seen as,' or 'is said to be.' It’s often used in formal or written contexts. The structure differs slightly depending on whether it’s used with a noun, adjective, or verb.
source_formation: Verb-casual + とされる / い-Adjective + とされる / な-Adjective + だとされる / Noun + だとされる

source_examples.japanese: サッカーは世界で最も人気のあるスポーツとされています。
source_examples.translation_en: Soccer is considered the most popular sport in the world.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は最も有能な科学者とされる。
source_examples.translation_en: He is considered the most talented scientist.

source_examples.japanese: この建物は地元のランドマークだとされています。
source_examples.translation_en: This building is said to be a local landmark.

source_examples.japanese: そのお寺は古代の美術品とされている。
source_examples.translation_en: That temple is considered an ancient work of art.

source_title: ～としたところで (〜to shita tokoro de)
source_short_explanation: Means 'even if' or 'even assuming'; emphasizes that the outcome won’t change.
source_long_explanation: The ～としたところで grammar point means 'even if' or 'even assuming that ~.' It highlights that even if the stated condition were met, the result would not significantly change. Often used to convey a sense of futility or skepticism in hypothetical statements.
source_formation: Verb-casual + としたところで / い-Adjective + としたところで / な-Adjective + だとしたところで / Noun + だとしたところで

source_examples.japanese: 彼が来るとしたところで、何も変わらないだろう。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if he comes, nothing will probably change.

source_examples.japanese: 美味しいお菓子を作るとしたところで、それが売れる保証はない。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if we make delicious sweets, there's no guarantee they’ll sell.

source_examples.japanese: 電話をかけるとしたところで、彼女が出るとは限らない。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if I call her, she might not pick up.

source_examples.japanese: 最高の材料を使うとしたところで、美味しくなるとは限らない。
source_examples.translation_en: Even if you use the best ingredients, it might not turn out delicious.

source_short_explanation: Expresses 'if', 'when', or 'assuming that' in a speculative sense.
source_long_explanation: The ～とすると grammar point is used for hypothetical or speculative situations, often in the sense of 'if we assume...', 'when it comes to...', or 'given that...' . It sets up a condition and then states the expected or possible outcome.
source_formation: Verb-casual + とすると / い-Adjective + とすると / な-Adjective + だとすると / Noun + だとすると

source_examples.japanese: 彼が来るとすると、もうすぐ到着するはずです。
source_examples.translation_en: If he’s coming, he should arrive soon.

source_examples.japanese: この仕事を終えるとすると、最低でも3日はかかるでしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: Assuming we finish this work, it will take at least three days.

source_examples.japanese: 戦争が起きるとすると、多くの人々が犠牲になるでしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: If a war were to break out, many people would become victims.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が経営者だとすると、多くの責任を負うことになるでしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: If he’s the manager, he will bear a lot of responsibility.

source_short_explanation: Used to express 'if it were the case that...', 'if we assume that...'.
source_long_explanation: The ～とすれば grammar point poses a hypothetical condition and then draws a conclusion or inference. It translates as 'if we suppose/assume that...' or 'if it is the case that...'.
source_formation: Verb-casual + とすれば / い-Adjective + とすれば / な-Adjective + だとすれば / Noun + だとすれば

source_examples.japanese: 彼が嘘つきだとすれば、その話は信じられない。
source_examples.translation_en: If he’s a liar, then his story can’t be believed.

source_examples.japanese: あなたが一緒に行くとすれば、私も行きます。
source_examples.translation_en: If you are going, I'll go too.

source_examples.japanese: 彼が浮気しているとすれば、どうすればいい？
source_examples.translation_en: If he’s cheating, what should I do?

source_examples.japanese: その薬が効かないとすれば、他の方法を試すべきだ。
source_examples.translation_en: If that medicine doesn’t work, we should try something else.

source_short_explanation: Used to express 'if it comes to...', 'when it becomes the case that...'.
source_long_explanation: The ～となったら grammar point is used to describe a situation where, if matters progress to that stage, a certain action or outcome will follow. It’s often translated as 'when it comes to...', 'if it comes to...'.
source_formation: Verb-casual + となったら / Noun + となったら

source_examples.japanese: 旅行に行くとなったら、荷造りをしなければいけません。
source_examples.translation_en: If it comes to going on a trip, we have to pack.

source_examples.japanese: 試験に落ちるとなったら、どうしよう。
source_examples.translation_en: What should I do if I fail the exam?

source_examples.japanese: 彼女と別れるとなったら、とても悲しいです。
source_examples.translation_en: If it comes to breaking up with her, I’ll be very sad.

source_examples.japanese: 結婚するとなったら、人生が大きく変わるでしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: When it comes to getting married, life will probably change drastically.

source_short_explanation: Used to highlight a certain circumstance; 'when it comes to...', 'if it becomes...', 'in the event that...'.
source_long_explanation: The ～となると grammar point highlights a specific situation or condition and indicates what normally or naturally happens under that circumstance. It can be translated as 'when it comes to...', 'if it becomes...', or 'in the event that...'.
source_formation: Verb-casual + となると / い-Adjective + となると / な-Adjective + だとなると / Noun + だとなると

source_examples.japanese: 試験となると、多くの学生が緊張する。
source_examples.translation_en: When it comes to exams, many students get nervous.

source_examples.japanese: 東京へ引っ越すとなると、生活費が一気に上がる。
source_examples.translation_en: If you move to Tokyo, the cost of living goes up drastically.

source_examples.japanese: 締め切りが明日となると、今夜は徹夜になりそうだ。
source_examples.translation_en: If the deadline is tomorrow, I’ll probably be up all night.

source_examples.japanese: 彼がリーダーとなると、チームの活動は大きく改善されるかもしれない。
source_examples.translation_en: If he becomes the leader, the team’s activities might improve significantly.

source_short_explanation: Expresses the idea of 'if it comes to...; when we talk about...; in the case of...'.
source_long_explanation: The ～となれば grammar point is used to express a situation where a particular case or condition brings about a certain result or consequence. It translates as 'if it comes to...; when we talk about...; in the case of...' in English.
source_formation: Verb-casual + となれば, い-Adjective + となれば, な-Adjective + だとなれば, Noun + だとなれば

source_examples.japanese: 彼がリーダーとなれば、プロジェクトは成功するでしょう。
source_examples.translation_en: If he becomes the leader, the project will probably succeed.

source_examples.japanese: 明日が雨だとなれば、ピクニックをキャンセルしましょう。
source_examples.translation_en: If it turns out to be raining tomorrow, let's cancel the picnic.

source_examples.japanese: この仕事が終わったとなれば、休暇を取ることができます。
source_examples.translation_en: If this job is over, you can take a vacation.

source_examples.japanese: そのテストが難しいとなれば、より一層勉強しなければならない。
source_examples.translation_en: If that test is difficult, we must study all the more.

source_short_explanation: Expresses something that the speaker heard; 'I've heard that', 'I was told that'.
source_long_explanation: The ～とのことだ grammar point is used to express something that the speaker has heard from someone else. It can be roughly translated as 'I've heard that', 'I was told that' in English. It is a formal way to present hearsay or information the speaker did not directly witness but was informed about.
source_formation: Simplified phrase + とのことだ

source_examples.japanese: 週末にパーティーがあるとのことだ。
source_examples.translation_en: I've heard that there is a party this weekend.

source_examples.japanese: 彼は来年ロンドンに引っ越すとのことだ。
source_examples.translation_en: I was told that he is moving to London next year.

source_examples.japanese: 彼女は新しい仕事についたとのことだ。
source_examples.translation_en: I've heard that she has gotten a new job.

source_examples.japanese: 明日は試験がないとのことだ。
source_examples.translation_en: I was told that there is no exam tomorrow.

source_short_explanation: Even though; although; but
